nodes.label: ABANDON
nodes.summary: Shall we indeed {abandon} our %STRING0 colony,
nodes.trigger: Player selects the Abandon-Colony command for an existing colony from the in-colony services menu.
nodes.inputs: The selected colony (its name is formatted into the prompt).
nodes.outputs: Confirm dialog 'Shall we indeed abandon our {colony} colony... forfeiting all of our hard work?' with 'Yes' / 'Never! That would be folly.' On Yes the colony is removed and all its accumulated work is lost.

nodes.label: ALREADYHAVE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} is set to produce a {%STRING1}, but
nodes.trigger: During the colony end-of-turn build/needs scan, the colony is set to produce a building it has already built.
nodes.inputs: Colony's queued building id matches a structure already present in the colony.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} is set to produce a {building}, but it has already built one!' (build queue flagged; no duplicate is built).

nodes.label: BUILT
nodes.summary: %STRING0 colony produces {%STRING1}.
nodes.trigger: A colonist is placed to work in (i.e. completes/activates) a colony building or structure; fires when the structure starts producing, for an interactive (human) colony.
nodes.inputs: The clicked/finished building id; the colony's per-(building,owner) tally is incremented; building != certain capacity-capped types.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} colony produces {product}.' and records this as the colony's last build. The colony's build-default work word is reset.

nodes.label: BURNED2
nodes.summary: Colony at {%STRING3} burned to the ground.
nodes.trigger: On resolving land combat where the attacker WINS against a target that is a colony, the colony is razed; BURNED2 is the spy-report variant reporting that a (foreign) colony was burned to the ground and its governor vows reprisals. Byte-cited in the win-flag tail of the land-combat decider (one of the three burn-outcome messages BURNED / BURNED2 / BURNED3).
nodes.inputs: Land-combat win against a colony tile (the target-is-colony flag set); attacker/colony nations formatted into the message.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Colony at {X} burned to the ground. {nation} governor vows reprisals.' The colony is destroyed (this is the observed/spy-report phrasing rather than the player's own-colony 'King demands explanation' wording).

nodes.label: COLLEGE2
nodes.summary: The {College} can support a faculty of only {two}
nodes.trigger: Player tries to assign more than two teachers in a colony whose school building is a College (the College faculty cap is 2).
nodes.inputs: Colony's school level == College; current teacher count already at 2.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'The College can support a faculty of only two teachers at a time'. The extra teacher assignment is rejected.

nodes.label: COLONY
nodes.summary: What shall we name this colony?
nodes.trigger: A new colony has just been founded by the active unit and the game asks the player to name it.
nodes.inputs: Newly created ColonyRecord with a default suggested name.
nodes.outputs: Name-entry prompt 'What shall we name this colony?'. The entered text becomes the colony name. (func_025D34 as listed is the colony-screen random-layout/graphics builder and is not itself the name-prompt emit site; trigger/outputs derived from the @COLONY message text and the colony-founding flow in func_022542.)

nodes.label: EFFICIENT
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has improved the efficiency of its government, Your Excellency.
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn SoL/Tory update, the colony's Tory (non-Sons-of-Liberty) share drops back below the inefficiency threshold, having previously been over it (the colony's inefficiency latch bit was set and now clears).
nodes.inputs: tory_count = population * (100 - rebel%) / 100; divisor = 10 - difficulty. EFFICIENT fires when tory_count is below the divisor and the colony's inefficiency flag was previously set. (The companion REBELMAJORITY 50-percent gate and this divisor model are byte-verified in the disassembly; same divisor used by the production penalty.)
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} has improved the efficiency of its government... Production penalties no longer apply'. The colony's -1-per-N-tories production penalty is removed.

nodes.label: EXTORTLAUGH
nodes.summary: "We laugh at your puny threats.  Do not try our patience, for
nodes.trigger: A player demands tribute/goods from a native village (an extortion attempt), but the village is strong/fierce enough to refuse defiantly. Byte-cited as the refuse branch of the native-village trade/extortion resolver that emits the EXTORTLAUGH message.
nodes.inputs: Demanding unit at the village; the village's resolve from the demand-vs-supply roll and the tribe's warrior strength; tribe name formatted into the message.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We laugh at your puny threats. Do not try our patience, for {tribe} warriors are known for their ferocity in times of war.' The demand yields nothing.

nodes.label: FOOD1
nodes.summary: Food stores have been depleted
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn food settlement, the colony's stored food has just been depleted (food stock reaches zero / goes negative) and it is NOT the pre-winter season.
nodes.inputs: Colony food stock after consuming population*2 this turn; season/turn threshold (the pre-winter latch at the year-threshold word is not yet set).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Food stores have been depleted in {colony}!' as a warning. (No starvation deaths yet this turn.)

nodes.label: FOOD2
nodes.summary: Food stores have been depleted
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn food settlement, food stores are depleted AND winter is coming soon (the pre-winter season threshold is met).
nodes.inputs: Colony food stock at/below zero; the season/year threshold indicating winter approaches.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Food stores have been depleted in {colony}! Winter is coming soon and we may starve to death!' (stronger warning than FOOD1).

nodes.label: FOODLOW
nodes.summary: The colony of {%STRING0} is rapidly depleting its
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn food settlement, the colony is rapidly depleting its food supply but still has some left (low-but-not-yet-empty band), heading into the winter months.
nodes.inputs: Remaining colony food stock (a small positive amount, passed as %NUMBER0 into the message).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'The colony of {X} is rapidly depleting its food supply... We have only {N food} left. We must have food for the winter months.'

nodes.label: FORTFIRE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} at {%STRING1} opens fire on {%STRING2 %STRING3}!
nodes.trigger: A colony with a coastal Fort/Fortress and at least one cannon (Artillery) garrisoned has an enemy (non-allied, non-treaty) combat unit move adjacent; the fort opens fire. Fires when computed firepower is greater than zero.
nodes.inputs: Fort/Fortress presence (one or two defenders with their bonus values); count of garrisoned cannon; the adjacent enemy unit. Firepower = cannon_count * fort_defenders * 4 (the multiply-by-four is byte-verified in the disassembly).
nodes.outputs: Shows '{Fort/Fortress} at {colony} opens fire on {enemy unit}!' and resolves a strike against the enemy via the land-combat decider (the target may be damaged/destroyed).

nodes.label: FULL
nodes.summary: The colony of {%STRING0} is {far too crowded},
nodes.trigger: Player tries to add an immigrant/colonist to a colony that is already at its maximum population (the colony is far too crowded).
nodes.inputs: Target colony population at the per-colony cap; the colony name is formatted into the message.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'The colony of {X} is far too crowded... find another colony for these immigrants'. The colonist is not placed.

nodes.label: KEEPSTOCKADE
nodes.summary: We cannot voluntarily reduce below {three} the population of a colony
nodes.trigger: Player tries to voluntarily reduce a colony's population below three (e.g. drag the last colonists out) while that colony has a stockade, fort, or fortress.
nodes.inputs: Colony has a stockade/fort/fortress AND the requested population would drop below 3.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We cannot voluntarily reduce below three the population of a colony that has a stockade, fort, or fortress'. The removal is blocked.

nodes.label: LANDFALL
nodes.summary: Shall we make landfall, Your Excellency,
nodes.trigger: A ship carrying land units reaches a coast tile and the player tries to move onto land (ship-destination status code 2: adjacent open land).
nodes.inputs: Active ship; destination tile classified as a normal landfall (status 2); the ship's secondary destination datum.
nodes.outputs: Confirm dialog 'Shall we make landfall, Your Excellency, and leave the ships behind?' with 'Stay With Ships' / 'Make Landfall'. On 'Make Landfall' the carried colonists are unloaded onto land and adjacent tiles are revealed.

nodes.label: LANDFALL2
nodes.summary: Our ships cannot navigate up this river,
nodes.trigger: A ship carrying land units tries to move into a tile it cannot reach by water (ship-destination status code 3: e.g. up a river the ship cannot navigate).
nodes.inputs: Active ship; destination tile classified as the river/inaccessible-landfall variant (status 3).
nodes.outputs: Confirm dialog 'Our ships cannot navigate up this river, Excellency. Shall we make landfall and leave the ships behind?' with 'Stay With Ships' / 'Make Landfall'. On 'Make Landfall' the carried units are unloaded onto land.

nodes.label: MORETHANTHREE
nodes.summary: We cannot put more than {three} colonists in any one building, Your
nodes.trigger: Player tries to place a fourth colonist into a single colony building (buildings hold at most three workers).
nodes.inputs: Target building already has 3 assigned colonists.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We cannot put more than three colonists in any one building'. The assignment is rejected.

nodes.label: NEEDCOLLEGE
nodes.summary: We must build a {college} to teach that
nodes.trigger: Player designates a teacher for a profession that the colony's current school (a Schoolhouse) is not advanced enough to teach (the profession requires a College). Dispatch arm where the colony's school field == College-required.
nodes.inputs: Selected teaching profession; colony school level below College; profession name formatted into the message.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We must build a college to teach that profession ({X}) in our colony'. The teaching assignment is rejected.

nodes.label: NEEDUNIVERSITY
nodes.summary: We must build a {university} to teach that
nodes.trigger: Player designates a teacher for a profession that requires a University while the colony's school is only a College/Schoolhouse. Dispatch arm where the colony's school field == University-required.
nodes.inputs: Selected teaching profession; colony school level below University; profession name formatted into the message.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We must build a university to teach that profession ({X}) in our colony'. The teaching assignment is rejected.

nodes.label: NOMOREWAREHOUSE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} is set to produce a {Warehouse Expansion},
nodes.trigger: Player sets a colony to build a Warehouse Expansion when it already has the maximum (only one expansion is allowed per colony; the colony's warehouse-level count is already at two).
nodes.inputs: Selected building is the warehouse expansion; the colony's warehouse-level count is already at its maximum of two (base warehouse plus one expansion).
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} is set to produce a Warehouse Expansion... but only one expansion is allowed per colony'. The build request is rejected.

nodes.label: NOTEACHER
nodes.summary: Only colonists who have mastered a profession may teach.
nodes.trigger: Player tries to set a colonist as a teacher in a school/college/university, but that colonist has no mastered profession to teach.
nodes.inputs: Selected colonist has no specialty profession.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Only colonists who have mastered a profession may teach'. The teacher assignment is rejected.

nodes.label: SCHOOL1
nodes.summary: The {Schoolhouse} can support a faculty of only {one}
nodes.trigger: Player tries to assign more than one teacher in a colony whose education building is a Schoolhouse (Schoolhouse faculty cap is 1).
nodes.inputs: Colony's school level == Schoolhouse; current teacher count already at 1.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'The Schoolhouse can support a faculty of only one teacher at a time'. The extra teacher assignment is rejected.

nodes.label: SCOUTCOLONY
nodes.summary: Our {scouts} have reached the outskirts of {%STRING0},
nodes.trigger: A Scout unit reaches the outskirts of a foreign (or other-power) colony and the player is offered scout actions against it.
nodes.inputs: The scout unit and the target colony (its name is shown in the prompt).
nodes.outputs: Action menu 'Our scouts have reached the outskirts of {colony}... What shall they do?' with 'Meet With Mayor' / 'Infiltrate Colony' / 'Attack Colony' / 'Nothing'. The chosen option drives the corresponding scout interaction. (Listed func_059B90 is ai_evaluate_unit_targets, the per-unit AI move/target scorer, which references but does not clearly emit this player-facing menu; trigger/outputs derived from the @SCOUTCOLONY message text, hence unverified.)

nodes.label: SEACOLONY
nodes.summary: It may surprise you to learn that colonies
nodes.trigger: Player issues Build-Colony ('B') with the active unit standing on a water/ocean tile (the tile has a sea 'feature' set).
nodes.inputs: Active unit's tile; feature_at_xy(unit) returns a water feature.
nodes.outputs: Refuses the colony. Shows the notice 'colonies cannot be built at sea'. No colony is founded; the unit keeps its move.

nodes.label: SONSDOWN
nodes.summary: Sons of Liberty membership in {%STRING0} is down to %NUMBER0%%, Your
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn SoL update, when no majority/minority band changed: the colony's Sons-of-Liberty percentage tens-band fell versus the previous sample (specifically (rebel%+4)/10 dropped below the prior tens-band), and the SoL-report option is enabled.
nodes.inputs: rebel% this turn vs previous turn; band = rebel%/10; gated by the 'Report Sons of Liberty membership' option being enabled.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Sons of Liberty membership in {colony} is down to {N} percent... Perhaps we should generate more Liberty Bells...' (informational; recommends Statesmen/Printing Press/Newspaper).

nodes.label: SONSUP
nodes.summary: Sons of Liberty membership in {%STRING0} is up to %NUMBER0%%, Your
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn SoL update, when no majority/minority band changed: the colony's Sons-of-Liberty percentage tens-band rose versus the previous sample, and the SoL-report option is enabled.
nodes.inputs: rebel% this turn vs previous turn; band_now = rebel%/10 greater than band_prev; gated by the 'Report Sons of Liberty membership' option being enabled.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Sons of Liberty membership in {colony} is up to {N} percent... The more Liberty Bells our Statesmen generate, the faster membership will rise.' (informational).

nodes.label: STARVE1
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} colony has run out of food, Your Excellency!
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn food settlement, the colony has run out of food during harsh winter weather and colonists die of starvation (winter band; not the 'winter coming' pre-warning).
nodes.inputs: Colony food stock exhausted while in the winter season band; one or more colonists are removed.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} colony has run out of food... many colonists are starving to death.' A colonist is removed from the colony (population drops).

nodes.label: STARVE2
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} colony has run out of food, Your Excellency!
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn food settlement, the colony has run out of food and colonists are starving, AND winter is still coming soon (the pre-winter threshold variant of the starvation band).
nodes.inputs: Colony food stock exhausted; season/year threshold indicating winter approaches; colonists removed.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} colony has run out of food... Colonists are starving to death, and to make matters worse, winter is coming soon.' A colonist is removed.

nodes.label: TOOMOUNTAIN
nodes.summary: Colonies cannot be built in the {mountains},
nodes.trigger: Build-Colony ('B') on a tile whose terrain id is mountains.
nodes.inputs: terrain_id_at_xy(unit) equals the mountains terrain id; the compare-then-show-TOOMOUNTAIN gate is byte-verified in the disassembly.
nodes.outputs: Refuses the colony. Shows 'Colonies cannot be built in the mountains'. Nothing is founded.

nodes.label: TOONEAR
nodes.summary: This land is too near to {%STRING0} for
nodes.trigger: Build-Colony ('B') on a tile that fails the colony-adjacency spacing check (an adjacency helper returns negative, or the colony-spacing flag is not 1), i.e. the tile is too close to an existing colony.
nodes.inputs: Adjacency/spacing check on the candidate tile; the message subject is set to the nearby colony's name.
nodes.outputs: Refuses the colony. Shows 'This land is too near to {colony} for a new colony'. Nothing is founded.

nodes.label: TOONEARBUILD
nodes.summary: A colony building project is already under way
nodes.trigger: Build-Colony ('B') where the 9-neighbour density scan finds a colony build project already under way in an adjacent square.
nodes.inputs: Neighbour scan over the 8 surrounding tiles detecting an in-progress colony-founding order.
nodes.outputs: Refuses the colony. Shows 'A colony building project is already under way in an adjacent square'. Nothing is founded.

nodes.label: TRAINCRIMINAL
nodes.summary: A {criminal} in {%STRING0} has become an {indentured
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn schooling step, a teacher graduates a Criminal one rank (the teacher-graduation path applied to a petty criminal), upgrading him.
nodes.inputs: Colony has an active teacher; a schooling candidate is a Criminal; the endgame report-suppression flag is clear.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'A criminal in {colony} has become an indentured servant through education.' The colonist's rank is upgraded Criminal -> Indentured Servant.

nodes.label: TRAINFAIL
nodes.summary: We have a {teacher} in {%STRING0}, but all the colonists
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn schooling step, there is a teacher in the colony but no eligible students: the schooling-candidate list emptied with no graduation because all colonists there already have specialty professions.
nodes.inputs: Colony has a teacher; schooling-candidate scan found no upgradeable colonist.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We have a teacher in {colony}, but all the colonists there already have specialty professions...' (suggests clearing a specialty). No graduation occurs.

nodes.label: TRAININDENTURED
nodes.summary: An {indentured servant} in {%STRING0} has become a
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn schooling step, a teacher graduates an Indentured Servant one rank (the indentured-servant graduation path), upgrading him to a free colonist.
nodes.inputs: Colony has an active teacher; a schooling candidate is an Indentured Servant.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'An indentured servant in {colony} has become a free colonist through education.' The colonist's rank is upgraded Indentured Servant -> Free Colonist.

nodes.label: TRAINPROFESSION
nodes.summary: A {colonist} in {%STRING0} has learned the specialty profession {%STRING1}.
nodes.trigger: On the colony end-of-turn schooling step, a teacher successfully teaches a Free Colonist (or convert-eligible colonist) a specialty profession. The teacher building's level (School/College/University -> band 4/6/8) determines which professions can be taught.
nodes.inputs: Colony has an active teacher whose profession can be taught at the colony's school level; an eligible student colonist; profession name formatted into the message.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'A colonist in {colony} has learned the specialty profession {X}.' The student gains that specialty profession.

nodes.label: TUTNOLUMBER
nodes.summary: None of the spaces surrounding this square are forested, Your Excellency.
nodes.trigger: Build-Colony ('B') on a difficulty/tutorial path where the surrounding squares contain no forest (the carpenters would have no lumber source).
nodes.inputs: Forest count in the colony's would-be work ring is zero; gated by the difficulty/tutorial-hints setting.
nodes.outputs: Shows a confirm dialog warning the colony will struggle for lumber, offering 'Cancel action' / 'Build colony anyway'. Founding proceeds only if the player confirms (choice == 'Build anyway').

nodes.label: TUTNOSPACES
nodes.summary: There are only a few productive squares adjacent to this square,
nodes.trigger: Build-Colony ('B') on a difficulty/tutorial path where only a few productive squares are adjacent (fewer than ~4 usable land tiles in the work ring).
nodes.inputs: Productive-land count in the colony's would-be work ring is low; gated by the difficulty/tutorial-hints setting.
nodes.outputs: Shows a confirm dialog warning of low growth potential, offering 'Cancel action' / 'Build colony anyway'. Founding proceeds only if confirmed.

nodes.label: UNREST
nodes.summary: Religious unrest in %COUNTRY causes increased
nodes.trigger: Religious unrest in the home country boosts emigration, making new colonists available on the Europe docks (a periodic Europe immigration event).
nodes.inputs: Home country (%COUNTRY); the made-available colonist type (%STRING1) and the home port name (%STRING0).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Religious unrest in {COUNTRY} causes increased emigration. Colonists ({type}) now available in {port}.' New recruits queue at the dock. (Listed func_033F6A is the page-trailing jump-table region after func_033C96 — a PHANTOM, not real code — so the emit site is not byte-traced here; trigger/outputs derived from the @UNREST message text, hence unverified.)

nodes.label: WAREHOUSEFULL
nodes.summary: Your Excellency, the warehouse at {%STRING0} already
nodes.trigger: Player unloads cargo from a unit into a colony (or otherwise adds a commodity) such that the resulting warehouse stock for that commodity would exceed the colony's storage capacity. Fires only for a non-food commodity when the dialog owner is interactive.
nodes.inputs: Commodity index (cargo != 0); current warehouse stock + amount being added; the colony's per-commodity capacity (smaller warehouses hold less). Byte-verified overflow check newstock > capacity in func_02A6A6.
nodes.outputs: Confirm popup: 'the warehouse at {X} already contains {N} units of {Y}. It can only hold {cap}. If we add another {K} units, some of the {Y} will probably spoil!' with 'Never mind' / 'Unload anyway'. Only on 'Unload anyway' is the stock added (which then triggers spoilage of the excess on the colony turn).

nodes.label: WORTHY
nodes.summary: "Although all of this land is rightfully ours by order of %STRING0,
nodes.trigger: During a European-power diplomacy meeting/parley, the other power proposes a demarcation ('line of Tordesillas') treaty dividing all the land into two perpetual spheres of influence. Byte-cited in the peace/treaty branch of the meeting dispatcher that emits the WORTHY message.
nodes.inputs: The two European powers (self and other); the proposing king's name (%STRING0); the two sphere labels (%STRING1, %STRING2).
nodes.outputs: Shows the demarcation-treaty offer 'we propose a demarcation treaty, dividing all the land... into perpetual and inviolable spheres of influence. Will you agree to such a partition?' with 'Yes' / 'No'. On Yes a sphere-of-influence partition treaty is established.

nodes.label: AMBUSHHINT
nodes.summary: Your Excellency, the King's armies have little experience with the
nodes.trigger: Per-power liberty-bell tick (func_03C322 = ff_bells_tick): during the revolution phase, the first time a power's accumulated bells cross the Continental-Congress threshold (game-phase bit0 set, bits1-2 clear, bells_toward_next > bells produced this turn), the 'Congress newly available' notification fires, printing the AMBUSHHINT combat-tip dialog (immediately followed by CONSIDER).
nodes.inputs: PowerRecord bells-toward-next-Father pool vs bells produced this turn; the game-phase flags (revolution-active bit, Congress-unlocked latch bits); bell threshold from ff_bells_required.
nodes.outputs: Hint dialog: when your troops attack the King's troops while NEITHER unit is in a colony square, you gain an ambush bonus equal to the terrain's normal defensive value. Sets game-phase bit2 (notified latch). Note: this is a tutorial/strategy tip, not a combat resolution.

nodes.label: ARTILLERY
nodes.summary: %STRING0 %STRING1 {damaged}.  Further damage will destroy it.
nodes.trigger: An Artillery unit (or Damaged Artillery) loses a land fight and the demotion ladder routes it to the destroy/damage block; specifically intact Artillery taking its first loss.
nodes.inputs: Loser UnitRecord is type Artillery; combat already decided (attacker won) by the land decider func_05CA7E; consequence applier func_05B2C2 reaches its destroy/damage block.
nodes.outputs: Intact Artillery is downgraded to Damaged Artillery (not destroyed). Shows 'X Artillery damaged. Further damage will destroy it.'.

nodes.label: ARTILLERY2
nodes.summary: Damaged %STRING0 %STRING1 {destroyed}.
nodes.trigger: A Damaged Artillery unit loses a land fight (its second loss).
nodes.inputs: Loser UnitRecord is type Damaged Artillery; combat decided against it.
nodes.outputs: The damaged artillery is destroyed and removed from the board. Shows 'Damaged X Artillery destroyed.'.

nodes.label: CAPTURED
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} march into {%STRING2}!  {%NUMBER0$}
nodes.trigger: An enemy (or, during the revolution, the King's) force successfully captures one of your colonies, plundering its treasury.
nodes.inputs: Attacking power; defending colony; gold in the colony treasury plundered. Resolved in the colony attack/capture path of the land decider func_05CA7E.
nodes.outputs: The colony changes hands and N gold is plundered. Shows 'X march into Z! {N} plundered!'.

nodes.label: CAPTURED2
nodes.summary: Spies report: {%STRING0} march into {%STRING2}.
nodes.trigger: Another power's colony is captured by a third party and you learn of it via spies (the spy-report variant of a colony capture, no plunder shown to you).
nodes.inputs: Attacking power; the foreign colony captured.
nodes.outputs: Spy report informs you the colony was taken. Shows 'Spies report: X march into Z.'.

nodes.label: CAPTURED3
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} march into {%STRING2}!
nodes.trigger: A colony you can directly observe is captured, but with no treasury to plunder (the no-plunder variant of a colony capture).
nodes.inputs: Attacking power; the captured colony (empty/no gold).
nodes.outputs: The colony changes hands; no gold message. Shows 'X march into Z!'.

nodes.label: CARGOCAPTURE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} cargo of {%NUMBER0 %STRING1} captured by {%STRING2 %STRING3}!
nodes.trigger: A ship attacker wins a ship-vs-ship fight and seizes a portion of the loser's cargo (ship-path spoils).
nodes.inputs: Winning ship; losing ship's cargo (commodity type + tonnage); ship-path roll already resolved in func_05B2C2.
nodes.outputs: A cargo of N units of a commodity is transferred to the victorious ship. Shows 'X cargo of {N commodity} captured by {Y ship}!'.

nodes.label: COLONISTCAPTURE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} colonists CAPTURED by the {%STRING1}!
nodes.trigger: A defenseless colonist-type unit (Free Colonist / specialist) is captured by an enemy combat unit (non-combatant capture path).
nodes.inputs: Loser is a colonist/non-combatant unit; capturing power.
nodes.outputs: The colonist(s) are captured by the enemy power. Shows 'X colonists CAPTURED by the Y!'.

nodes.label: COLONISTCAPTURE2
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} colonists CAPTURED by the {%STRING1}!  Soldiers
nodes.trigger: A Veteran Soldier loses and is captured/reduced, also stripping veteran status (the capture branch that emits the 'lose Veteran status' variant).
nodes.inputs: Loser is a (veteran) soldier whose capture reduces it to colonist; capturing power.
nodes.outputs: The colonist(s) captured AND the soldier loses Veteran status. Shows 'X colonists CAPTURED by the Y! Soldiers lose Veteran status.'.

nodes.label: COUNTRIES
nodes.summary: the Holy Roman Empire
nodes.trigger: Filler/lookup table of non-playable nation names used when a message needs to name a foreign (king's-enemy) country, e.g. for KINGNEWWAR / war-declaration text.
nodes.inputs: An index selecting one of the listed countries; pulled by the king/war message builders (func_033F6A area).
nodes.outputs: Supplies one country name from the fixed list: the Holy Roman Empire, the Portuguese, the Ottoman Turks, the Barbary Pirates, Russia, Prussia, Sweden, Denmark. Not an event in itself; substituted into combat/war narration.

nodes.label: DEMOTE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0 %STRING1} routed!  Unit demoted to {%STRING2} status.
nodes.trigger: A combatant land unit loses a fight on open ground (no colony/fort present) and has a defined demotion target on the fixed ladder.
nodes.inputs: Loser UnitRecord type; fixed remap ladder (byte-verified in func_05B2C2): Dragoon->Soldier, Soldier->Free Colonist, Continental Cavalry->Continental Army, Continental Army->Free Colonist, Cavalry->Regular; a veteran-status override (vet_type==24) remaps a 0-outcome to Expert-class 3 instead. Types with no ladder entry are destroyed outright (no DEMOTE message).
nodes.outputs: Loser's unit type is changed to the next-lower rung; the unit survives. Shows 'X Y routed! Unit demoted to Z status.'.

nodes.label: GIVECASH
nodes.summary: "Please spare our meek and helpless settlement from destruction.
nodes.trigger: A weak/helpless settlement (native village or other) offers a cash bribe to a stronger attacker to be spared, just before an attack would resolve. Surfaced in the European/native diplomacy meeting dispatcher func_057F4E (paid-peace MEEK/GIVECASH branch).
nodes.inputs: Defender's available gold (the offered amount, computed from the other power's gold scaled by a difficulty/strength factor x100); whether the parties are not already at war.
nodes.outputs: Y/N dialog offering N gold for peace/sparing. Accepting transfers N gold from the defender to the player and sets a peace/treaty bit; declining proceeds with the attack.

nodes.label: HALF
nodes.summary: Your Excellency, these men are tired.  If we force
nodes.trigger: A unit with too few movement/action points left is ordered to attack this turn anyway; the game warns it will fight at reduced strength and asks for confirmation.
nodes.inputs: Acting unit's remaining action capacity (soft_score < 3 in the leaf); the fraction-of-strength figure (N/3) it would fight at. Evaluated in the func_05CA7E head.
nodes.outputs: Y/N prompt 'these men are tired... they will fight at {N/3 strength}.' Choosing Charge commits the weakened attack (attacker strength is scaled by soft_score/3 in the combat math); choosing rest aborts the attack.

nodes.label: LOOTCAPTURE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} treasure worth {%NUMBER0$} CAPTURED by the {%STRING1}!
nodes.trigger: A Treasure unit is captured when an enemy combat unit defeats/overruns its stack (the non-combatant capture path).
nodes.inputs: Loser is a Treasure-carrying unit (non-combatant type); capturing power; treasure value carried by the unit.
nodes.outputs: The treasure (worth N gold) is seized by the capturing power. Shows 'X treasure worth {N} CAPTURED by the Y!'.

nodes.label: PIRACY
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 is most displeased with the {%STRING1 pirates} lying
nodes.trigger: Another European power (or the King) demands you withdraw your Privateers that are lurking off their coast, during a diplomacy parley. War-grievance exchange in func_057F4E (gated on a contact bit and the offended power having a colony/strength).
nodes.inputs: Presence of your Privateers near the complaining power's coast; the request/demand verb (MEEKNESS) chosen by their attitude.
nodes.outputs: Dialog demanding withdrawal of all Privateers. Choosing to comply withdraws them to Europe and clears the war high-bit; denying piracy keeps them and risks war.

nodes.label: SHIPCOMBAT
nodes.summary: Only {Privateers} and {Frigates} can attack enemy ships.
nodes.trigger: Player orders a non-warship (or any ship that is not a Privateer/Frigate) to attack an enemy ship, or a ship move resolves to the 'cannot attack ships' status. Dispatched in the ship move/arrival handler func_03FDDE (destination status case 7).
nodes.inputs: Active ship's type; destination classified by func_03FA9C which writes the ship-dest status code.
nodes.outputs: Refusal message: 'Only Privateers and Frigates can attack enemy ships.'. The attack is not performed.

nodes.label: SHIPSUNK
nodes.summary: {%STRING0 %STRING1 sunk} by %STRING2 %STRING3!
nodes.trigger: A ship loses a ship-vs-ship fight badly enough to be sunk (ship-path destroy branch). Per the ship roll, the attacking ship wins iff roll<=hull, and a losing defender with no repair option sinks.
nodes.inputs: Loser ship type + name; victor ship type + name; ship roll on guns(DEF)/hull(ATK).
nodes.outputs: The ship is destroyed (sunk) with all cargo lost. Shows 'X Y sunk by Z W!'.

nodes.label: SIEGE
nodes.summary: This colony is under {siege}, since enemy combat units
nodes.trigger: Player tries to create/train a non-military unit in a colony that is under siege (enemy combat units in the surrounding area outnumber friendly combat units).
nodes.inputs: Colony's surrounding-area combat-unit balance (enemy vs friendly). Gated in the colony-management overlay func_02883E.
nodes.outputs: Refusal message: while besieged, only Soldier and Dragoon units may be created in this colony. Shows the SIEGE notice; no unit is created.

nodes.label: SIEGES
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 is disturbed by the large %STRING1 forces lurking
nodes.trigger: Another power demands you withdraw the large military force you have stationed adjacent to their colonies, during a diplomacy parley (SIEGES exchange in func_057F4E).
nodes.inputs: Count of your military units adjacent to the complaining power's colonies vs their tolerance threshold; the request/demand verb.
nodes.outputs: Dialog demanding withdrawal of all units adjacent to their colonies. Complying withdraws your forces to Europe; refusing keeps them (and lowers their attitude / risks war).

nodes.label: VALOR
nodes.summary: Because of their valor in battle, our {%STRING0}
nodes.trigger: A soldier-class unit wins a land fight and is promoted up the combat ladder (the generic promotion case in the post-combat FX routine, reached on a combat WIN).
nodes.inputs: Winning UnitRecord; its current class and next class; called from the land decider's win branch (func_05CA7E -> func_05C69C post-combat FX). Reaches the generic 'promoted from X to Y' branch (the non-Veteran, non-Continental case).
nodes.outputs: The unit's type advances one promotion rung. Shows 'Because of their valor in battle, our X soldiers have been promoted from Y to Z status.'.

nodes.label: WAGONCAPTURE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} wagon train CAPTURED by the {%STRING1}!
nodes.trigger: A Wagon Train unit is captured when an enemy combat unit defeats it (non-combatant capture path).
nodes.inputs: Loser is a Wagon Train (non-combatant type); capturing power.
nodes.outputs: The wagon train (and any cargo) is captured by the enemy power. Shows 'X wagon train CAPTURED by the Y!'.

nodes.label: BADCARGO
nodes.summary: "We have enough {%STRING0} and don't
nodes.trigger: While trading at a native settlement, the player offers (to sell) a commodity the village already has plenty of, so the natives decline that good and counter with what they actually want.
nodes.inputs: The offered commodity (STRING0); the tribe's current stocks of that good; up to three goods the village does want (STRING1, STRING2, STRING3) drawn from its demand list.
nodes.outputs: Shows the natives' refusal: they have enough of STRING0 and ask the player to come back with STRING1/STRING2 (even STRING3 would help). No trade occurs; the player may pick a different good.

nodes.label: BURNED3
nodes.summary: Spies report: {%STRING0} burn {%STRING1} colony at {%STRING3}.
nodes.trigger: During the combat decider, when the resolved target was an enemy colony that gets burned, the spies-report variant fires to notify the player that one rival European power has burned another rival's colony (third-party report).
nodes.inputs: The attacking power that burned the colony (STRING0); the victim power (STRING1) and the colony location (STRING3); the combat win flag and the 'target is a colony' flag.
nodes.outputs: Posts a spies-report notice: '<attacker> burn <victim> colony at <place>. <victim> governor vows reprisals.' Informational; the colony-loss/loot is applied in the combat tail.

nodes.label: BUY0
nodes.summary: "We shall fill up your {%STRING1} with {%NUMBER2 %STRING0} in
nodes.trigger: While trading at a native settlement on the BUY path, the player chooses to buy a good the village has, and the natives quote an asking price to fill the unit's hold.
nodes.inputs: The good being bought (STRING0); the carrying unit and its empty hold (STRING1); quantity offered (NUMBER2); the native ask price (NUMBER0) and the player's available gold (NUMBER3); a fairer counter price (NUMBER1); the buyer power's PowerRecord gold.
nodes.outputs: Shows the offer to fill the hold with NUMBER2 of STRING0 for NUMBER0 gold, with choices to pay, counter-offer (NUMBER1), or decline. On accept (and if affordable) the buyer's PowerRecord gold is debited by the ask and the goods load into the unit; if unaffordable a NOTENOUGH refusal is raised.

nodes.label: CARGOLOAD
nodes.summary: Select a cargo to load at {%STRING0}.
nodes.trigger: The cargo/stack-row UI is drawn in LOAD mode at a colony (the stack-row layout handler picks the load title), prompting the player to choose which cargo to load onto a transport.
nodes.inputs: The colony (STRING0 = name); the layout mode flag that selects the load title; the unit stack/cargo rows at the cursor.
nodes.outputs: Presents the prompt 'Select a cargo to load at <colony>.' and lets the player pick a commodity row to load into the ship/wagon hold.

nodes.label: CARGOREADY0
nodes.summary: A new cargo of {%STRING1} is ready at {%STRING0}, Your Excellency.
nodes.trigger: During the per-colony end-of-turn update, a colony has accumulated a fresh, exportable load of a commodity (the new-cargo report event, gated by the colony's production/build state and the 'report new cargos available' option).
nodes.inputs: The colony (STRING0 = colony name) and the commodity that just became available (STRING1 = cargo name); the colony's per-turn production and warehouse state.
nodes.outputs: Posts a turn-report notice: 'A new cargo of <commodity> is ready at <colony>, Your Excellency.' Informational only; no resource change beyond the production already booked.

nodes.label: CARGOUNLOAD
nodes.summary: Select a cargo to unload at {%STRING0}.
nodes.trigger: The cargo/stack-row UI is drawn in UNLOAD mode at a colony (the stack-row layout handler picks the unload title), prompting the player to choose which cargo to unload from a transport.
nodes.inputs: The colony (STRING0 = name); the layout mode flag that selects the unload title; the unit stack/cargo rows at the cursor.
nodes.outputs: Presents the prompt 'Select a cargo to unload at <colony>.' and lets the player pick a commodity row to discharge from the ship/wagon hold into the colony.

nodes.label: DEFICIT
nodes.summary: "Since you have brought no trade goods, we will not
nodes.trigger: The player initiates trade at a native settlement with a unit that is carrying no trade goods at all, so there is nothing to sell.
nodes.inputs: The trading unit and its (empty) cargo hold; the native settlement.
nodes.outputs: Shows the natives' refusal: 'Since you have brought no trade goods, we will not trade with you.' The trade session ends with no exchange.

nodes.label: DISBANDSHIP
nodes.summary: We cannot disband a ship at sea while it is carrying
nodes.trigger: Player issues the Disband command ('D') on a ship that is currently at sea while it still has more than one unit/cargo aboard. The disband handler classifies the target as a ship (ship-class unit type) and counts what it is carrying.
nodes.inputs: The targeted ship unit; the count of units/cargo loaded aboard it (must be greater than one to block).
nodes.outputs: Shows a message refusing the disband ('We cannot disband a ship at sea while it is carrying units') and aborts. The ship is NOT destroyed; no further disband prompt is shown.

nodes.label: EUROPELOSE
nodes.summary: {%STRING1 %STRING2} %STRING4 {%STRING0} near %STRING3!
nodes.trigger: A combat between the active power and a rival EUROPEAN power's unit/colony resolves as a loss for the active power (the combat decider's win flag is zero).
nodes.inputs: The attacker unit and defender; the resolved win flag (zero = loss); the units' nationalities, types, and the engagement location (STRING0..STRING4 fill the result line).
nodes.outputs: Shows the loss line (e.g. '<enemy nation> <enemy unit> <verb> <our unit> near <place>!') and the consequence applier removes/demotes the active power's attacking unit.

nodes.label: EUROPESHIPOPTIONS
nodes.summary: Move to front.
nodes.trigger: Player clicks a ship docked in the Europe port screen; the Europe ship-interaction handler builds and presents that ship's command menu.
nodes.inputs: The clicked ship's UnitRecord index and type; the ship's cargo-slot state; the per-type stat row used to format the ship label.
nodes.outputs: Presents the Europe-port ship menu: Move to front, Set sail for the New World, Unload all cargo, No changes. Selecting 'Set sail' dispatches the ship out of Europe toward the New World; 'Unload' empties its hold in port.

nodes.label: EUROPEWIN
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} %STRING4 {%STRING1 %STRING2} near %STRING3!
nodes.trigger: A combat between the active power and a rival EUROPEAN power's unit/colony resolves as a win for the active power (the combat decider's win flag is nonzero).
nodes.inputs: The attacker unit and defender; the resolved win flag (nonzero = win); the units' nationalities, types, and the engagement location (STRING0..STRING4 fill the result line).
nodes.outputs: Shows the win line (e.g. '<our nation> <verb> <enemy nation> <enemy unit> near <place>!') and the consequence applier removes/demotes the defender (or, for a colony target, proceeds to the burn/loot path).

nodes.label: INEFFICIENT
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has an inefficient government, Your Excellency!
nodes.trigger: During the per-colony end-of-turn update, the number of colonists who are NOT Sons of Liberty members (the tory count) reaches or exceeds the inefficiency band, where the band size is (10 minus difficulty level). Reported once when the colony crosses into the inefficient state (latched), if the 'report inefficient government' option is on.
nodes.inputs: Colony population; rebel (Sons of Liberty) percentage; tory_count = population x (100 - rebel_pct) / 100; difficulty level (sets the threshold = 10 - difficulty); the colony's already-reported flag and the report-option bit.
nodes.outputs: Posts a warning that the colony has an inefficient government: every group of NUMBER0 tories beyond the threshold imposes a -1 production penalty on its colonists. The penalty itself is applied in the production model; this is the notification. Sets the colony's 'inefficient already reported' flag.

nodes.label: MADATSHIPS
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} people do not trust the men in your
nodes.trigger: A ship-class unit (ship/galleon/man-of-war range) approaches a settlement of a power whose relation flag indicates distrust of the player's fleet, and the anger/relation thresholds are crossed, so that power refuses sea contact. (Message text is verified; the handler's exact King-versus-fleet vs native-distrust framing is not fully pinned down.)
nodes.inputs: The arriving ship unit and its owner nibble; the other power and its relation flags toward the player; the per-power distrust/anger state word and threshold; the relevant PowerRecord gold for the intervention branch.
nodes.outputs: Shows the refusal: 'The <power> people do not trust the men in your ships... If you approach our shoreline we shall punish you.' The trade/contact is refused, with a possible hostile reprisal if the ship continues toward shore.

nodes.label: NODOCKS
nodes.summary: We cannot operate fishing boats at this colony
nodes.trigger: In the colony-services menu, the player selects an action that would operate fishing boats / load from the water at a colony that has not yet built Docks (menu dispatch item that maps to the no-docks branch).
nodes.inputs: The selected colony and its building set (specifically whether Docks is present); the chosen menu item id.
nodes.outputs: Shows an informational popup explaining that fishing boats cannot operate at this colony until Docks is built. No state change; the action is refused.

nodes.label: NOPORT
nodes.summary: This square does not have access to the {ocean},
nodes.trigger: Player issues the Build-Colony command ('B') on a tile that has no ocean square adjacent to it. The build-colony validity check reaches the port/access gate and finds the chosen tile is landlocked.
nodes.inputs: The active land unit and its map tile; the 8 neighbouring tiles tested for adjacency to ocean water; current difficulty/tutorial setting (the port gate is one of the difficulty-gated build checks).
nodes.outputs: Shows a confirm dialog warning that the colony would have no ocean access, so its produce must be hauled to a port by wagon trains. The player may confirm (build anyway) or cancel. No game state changes until confirmation.

nodes.label: PRICEDOWN
nodes.summary: The price of {%STRING0} in %STRING1 has fallen to {%NUMBER0$}.
nodes.trigger: During the market price-drift recompute, a commodity's accumulated supply crosses its fall threshold so its European price ticks down by one, and the affected market belongs to a human-controlled (non-AI) power so the change is announced.
nodes.inputs: The commodity (STRING0 = cargo name); the European market/nation (STRING1 = nation name); the commodity's per-good fall parameters from the cargo data table; the per-good demand accumulator and current price level versus its floor; the active power and whether it is AI-controlled.
nodes.outputs: Lowers the commodity's European price by one (clamped above its per-good floor), subtracts the fall threshold from the accumulator, and posts a notice: 'The price of <commodity> in <nation> has fallen to <new price>.'

nodes.label: PRICEUP
nodes.summary: The price of {%STRING0} in %STRING1 has risen to {%NUMBER0$}.
nodes.trigger: During the market price-drift recompute, a commodity's accumulated demand crosses its rise threshold so its European price ticks up by one, and the affected market belongs to a human-controlled (non-AI) power so the change is announced.
nodes.inputs: The commodity (STRING0 = cargo name); the European market/nation (STRING1 = nation name); the commodity's per-good attrition/rise parameters from the cargo data table; the per-good demand accumulator and current price level versus its ceiling; the active power and whether it is AI-controlled.
nodes.outputs: Raises the commodity's European sell/buy price by one (clamped below its per-good ceiling), subtracts the rise threshold from the demand accumulator, and posts a notice: 'The price of <commodity> in <nation> has risen to <new price>.'

nodes.label: ROUTELOOP
nodes.summary: Your Excellency, our "{%STRING0}" trade route
nodes.trigger: A unit assigned to a named trade route arrives and the route-arrival check finds the route effectively has only one port on its itinerary (all candidate stops resolve to the same destination), so the unit cannot continue.
nodes.inputs: The trade-route name (STRING0); the unit's home colony / route stop list; the per-slot production snapshot the arrival check compares (all-equal means a single effective port).
nodes.outputs: Opens a panel and shows 'Your Excellency, our "<route>" trade route has only one port on its itinerary!' then ends the unit's activity. The unit halts rather than looping.

nodes.label: SAILHOME
nodes.summary: We have reached the {high seas}, Your
nodes.trigger: A player ship reaches the high-seas edge of the map (the destination-classifier returns the sail-home status for the move). Only asked when the ship is NOT already locked in Europe; if it is, the EUROPENOTLEAVE refusal is shown instead.
nodes.inputs: The active ship and its computed destination tile; the destination status code from the ship-destination classifier; the in-Europe lock flag.
nodes.outputs: Asks 'We have reached the high seas... Shall we sail for Europe?' with Yes/No. On Yes the ship departs the map for Europe (enters the trans-Atlantic crossing); on No it stays in coastal waters and the move is abandoned.

nodes.label: SHIPDAMAGE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0 %STRING1} damaged!  Ship returns to {%STRING2} for repairs.
nodes.trigger: A ship loses a naval combat but is damaged rather than sunk (the ship-path LOSE branch of the combat consequence applier, when the elimination flag selects damage).
nodes.inputs: The losing ship (STRING0 = nationality, STRING1 = ship type); the friendly port it retreats to (STRING2); the combat outcome flags selecting damage versus sinking.
nodes.outputs: Shows '<nation> <ship> damaged! Ship returns to <port> for repairs.' The ship survives but is sent back to a friendly port and is out of action while repairing (its cargo/load handling follows the damage path; SHIPSUNK is the alternative when destroyed).

nodes.label: SHIPLAKE
nodes.summary: Ship units cannot enter inland {lake} squares.
nodes.trigger: A player ship attempts to move into an inland lake square; the ship-destination classifier returns the lake status for the destination tile.
nodes.inputs: The active ship and its destination tile; the destination status code identifying the tile as an inland lake.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Ship units cannot enter inland lake squares.' and refuses the move; the ship stays put.

nodes.label: SHIPOPTIONS
nodes.summary: Move to front.
nodes.trigger: Player opens the unit-orders popup for a ship (in a colony garrison or harbour). The order-menu builder presents the ship's available commands.
nodes.inputs: The selected ship unit and its current activity/orders byte and type (used to enable/disable individual menu items).
nodes.outputs: Presents a list of ship orders: Move to front, Clear orders, Sentry, Anchor in harbor ('Fortify'), Unload all cargo, No changes. The chosen item then sets the unit's activity (wake / sentry / fortify), unloads cargo, or commits a board/load move.

nodes.label: SHIPRUN
nodes.summary: {%STRING2 %STRING0} slips past {%STRING1 %STRING3}!
nodes.trigger: A ship moving through waters watched by an enemy ship successfully evades the blockading/intercepting vessel (the 'slips past' naval-interception outcome). Derived from the message text; the emitting code path is not reconstructed in the ported source.
nodes.inputs: The moving ship (STRING0) and its nationality (STRING2); the enemy interceptor ship (STRING3) and its nationality (STRING1).
nodes.outputs: Posts a notice: '<nation> <ship> slips past <enemy nation> <enemy ship>!' The moving ship continues its voyage unhindered.

nodes.label: SHIPSLOW
nodes.summary: {%STRING0}'s progress slowed by presence of {%STRING1 %STRING2}.
nodes.trigger: A ship's sea movement is reduced because an enemy ship is present in/near its path (the interception that slows rather than stops the voyage). Derived from the message text; the emitting code path is not reconstructed in the ported source.
nodes.inputs: The moving ship (STRING0); the enemy ship slowing it (STRING2) and its nationality (STRING1).
nodes.outputs: Posts a notice: '<ship>'s progress slowed by presence of <enemy nation> <enemy ship>.' The ship's remaining movement for the turn is curtailed.

nodes.label: SMITEEUROPE
nodes.summary: "We shall ruthlessly drive the heretic {%STRING0}
nodes.trigger: At a native settlement, the player asks the tribe to attack a rival EUROPEAN power (the smite branch targeting another colonial nation rather than a native tribe). The tribe quotes a gold fee to do it.
nodes.inputs: The target rival European power (STRING0 = its name); the tribe being asked; a computed gold fee (NUMBER0) derived from the tribe's treasury and a player factor, optionally halved by a PowerRecord bit; the player power's PowerRecord gold.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We shall ruthlessly drive the heretic <power> from the New World in exchange for <fee> to cover our expenses.' with Pay / Never mind. On Pay (if affordable) the tribe's gold is debited and the player's PowerRecord gold receives the transfer, and the tribe is set to war against the named European power; if the tribe is too poor an UNFORTUNATE refusal is shown instead.

nodes.label: SPOIL1
nodes.summary: The colony of {%STRING0} has exceeded its warehouse capacity.
nodes.trigger: During the per-colony end-of-turn update, a colony's stockpile of a single commodity exceeds its warehouse capacity and the exact overflow tonnage of that one commodity is known, so the precise spoilage is reported.
nodes.inputs: The colony (STRING0 = name); the commodity that overflowed (STRING1 = cargo name); the warehouse capacity; the overflow amount (NUMBER0 = tons thrown away).
nodes.outputs: Posts a notice that the colony exceeded warehouse capacity and NUMBER0 tons of <commodity> were thrown away, hinting that a larger warehouse holds another 100 tons. The overflow stock is discarded down to capacity.

nodes.label: SPOIL2
nodes.summary: The colony of {%STRING0} has exceeded its warehouse capacity.
nodes.trigger: During the per-colony end-of-turn update, a colony's stockpile exceeds warehouse capacity but multiple commodities overflowed (no single tonnage is named), so the generic spoilage message is shown instead of SPOIL1.
nodes.inputs: The colony (STRING0 = name); the set of commodities over capacity; the warehouse capacity.
nodes.outputs: Posts a notice that the colony exceeded warehouse capacity and some cargo was thrown away, hinting that a larger warehouse holds another 100 tons. The overflowing stock is discarded down to capacity.

nodes.label: TRADE0
nodes.summary: "We see that you have brought some %STRING0
nodes.trigger: While trading at a native settlement on the SELL path, the unit carries a commodity the village wants, and the natives quote a gold offer to buy it.
nodes.inputs: The commodity carried (STRING1) and its descriptor (STRING0); the native buy offer (NUMBER0); a fairer counter price (NUMBER1); the selling power's PowerRecord gold.
nodes.outputs: Shows the natives' purchase offer for the goods with choices: accept NUMBER0, counter-offer NUMBER1, gift the goods (no payment), or decline. On accept the seller's PowerRecord gold is credited by the agreed total and the cargo is removed from the unit.

nodes.label: TRADEMERCANTILISM
nodes.summary: "In the interests of {Mercantilism}, %STRING0 has ordered us not
nodes.trigger: The player tries to trade goods with another European power's settlement, but that power's monarch has imposed Mercantilism (the mercantilism check for the foreign power returns set), forbidding trade with foreign merchants.
nodes.inputs: The trading unit and the foreign power's owner nibble; that power's leader (STRING0 = monarch/leader name); the mercantilism flag for that power; the at-peace/treaty relation bit (a separate TRADEATWAR refusal applies if not at peace).
nodes.outputs: Shows '<leader> has ordered us not to trade with foreign merchants... we must ask you to go away.' and aborts the trade dialog with no exchange.

nodes.label: TRADENAMES
nodes.trigger: Not a triggered popup but a data name-list the game reads when displaying or labelling trade-route types. Referenced wherever a trade-route's behaviour type is named. (Body emitting it is not reconstructed in the ported source; meaning derived from the list text.)
nodes.inputs: A trade-route type index (0..4) used to select one of the five names.
nodes.outputs: Supplies the five trade-route type labels: Run, Ferry, Cargo, Transport, Triangle. Used as display strings for route configuration; no game-state change of its own.

nodes.label: TRADENOCARGO
nodes.summary: "You have brought nothing with you to trade with us.  Please come
nodes.trigger: The player opens the trade-with-foreign-power dialog with a unit that is carrying no cargo, so there is nothing to offer (the unit's cargo-slot count is zero).
nodes.inputs: The trading unit and its (empty) cargo-slot count; the foreign power (already passed the at-peace and mercantilism gates).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'You have brought nothing with you to trade with us. Please come back when you have something useful to offer.' and aborts the trade dialog.

nodes.label: UNIV3
nodes.summary: The {University} can support a faculty of only {three}
nodes.trigger: In the colony-services menu, the player tries to add a fourth teacher to a University whose faculty is already at its cap of three teachers (training/schooling menu branch).
nodes.inputs: The selected colony; its University building level; the current count of assigned teachers (cap is three).
nodes.outputs: Shows an informational popup that a University supports only three teachers at a time. The assignment is refused; no colonist is added as a teacher.

nodes.label: BADHAGGLE2
nodes.summary: "Our patience with your haggling is exhausted.
nodes.trigger: When BUYING a good from a native settlement, the player haggles too aggressively and exhausts the tribe's patience; the natives refuse to sell anything further until the player brings something of value.
nodes.inputs: Haggle-escalation state in the native trade resolver func_049600 (the BUY-side patience-exhausted state); the player's offer history this session.
nodes.outputs: 'Our patience with your haggling is exhausted. We will sell you nothing further until you bring us something of value.'. Sale aborted; the settlement is flagged unwilling to sell.

nodes.label: BADHAGGLE3
nodes.summary: "As we said before, we will sell you nothing further
nodes.trigger: The player re-approaches a native settlement that already refused to sell (BADHAGGLE2 state) and tries to buy again without having brought anything new.
nodes.inputs: The settlement's already-refused sell state; the player's (still empty-handed) approach. Native trade resolver func_049600.
nodes.outputs: 'As we said before, we will sell you nothing further until you bring us something of value.'. No sale.

nodes.label: BUYWHICH
nodes.summary: "We have {%STRING0}, {%STRING1}, and {%STRING2} available to trade with
nodes.trigger: A scout/wagon arrives at a native settlement willing to sell, and the game presents the menu of goods the tribe has available to buy.
nodes.inputs: The three commodities the settlement currently offers for sale (data-driven by the settlement). Native trade resolver func_049600.
nodes.outputs: Menu: 'We have {A}, {B}, and {C} available to trade with you. Which would you like to buy?' with the three goods plus 'Nothing'. Selecting one proceeds to the BUY0/BUY1 price-haggle dialog.

nodes.label: CASHTREASURE
nodes.summary: Treasure sold to foreign agents for {%NUMBER0$}.
nodes.trigger: A Treasure unit is sold to foreign agents (cashed in without shipping it home via a galleon), or, in the demo/endgame fast path, treasure is auto-converted; resolved in the treasure-transport event func_05C878.
nodes.inputs: Treasure base value = 100 x settlement size; a tax/share multiplier M (capped at 90; for the non-pirate case M = max((player_difficulty+10)*5, pool*2)); gold_delta = M * base / 100. Attacker PowerRecord.
nodes.outputs: Treasure is sold for N gold, credited to the power's treasury; the remaining (base - gold_delta) accrues to total-loot and score-bonus. Shows 'Treasure sold to foreign agents for {N}.'.

nodes.label: NOTHINGWITHDRAW
nodes.summary: "We have no forces adjacent to your colonies."
nodes.trigger: During a parley you ask another power to withdraw their forces from near your colonies, but they have no forces adjacent to your colonies. Diplomacy WITHDRAW block of func_057F4E.
nodes.inputs: Count of the other power's units adjacent to your colonies == 0.
nodes.outputs: 'We have no forces adjacent to your colonies.'. No action.

nodes.label: VANISH
nodes.summary: Your Excellency!  Our colony at {%STRING0} has
nodes.trigger: A colony runs completely out of food during the colony turn update and all its colonists starve, eliminating the colony.
nodes.inputs: Colony food stockpile reaching zero with no production. Detected in the colony turn-update path func_02D658.
nodes.outputs: The colony is destroyed. Shows 'Our colony at X has vanished! The colonists appear to have starved to death.'.

nodes.label: WELLSEASONED
nodes.summary: Our {Scouts} have improved to {Seasoned} status, Your Excellency.
nodes.trigger: A Scout improves from base to Seasoned status (a scout-specific promotion, emitted from the native-village / exploration interaction path).
nodes.inputs: Scout unit; the seasoning-promotion condition (e.g. successful exploration / chief interaction). Emitted in func_04A7CA (chief/village interaction).
nodes.outputs: The scout's class advances to Seasoned. Shows 'Our Scouts have improved to Seasoned status, Your Excellency.'.

nodes.label: HELLOUSA
nodes.summary: "Greetings, %STRING0, from the newly elected government
nodes.trigger: You begin a diplomacy parley with another European power that has WON its independence and become a 'United States'-style republic; the post-independence greeting variant is selected. Greeting block of the European-diplomacy meeting dispatcher func_057F4E.
nodes.inputs: The other power's post-revolution (independent) state; greeting-variant selector (chooses HELLOUSA over HELLOFIRST/HELLOAHOY/HELLOMEEK/HELLOMANLY).
nodes.outputs: Greeting line: 'Greetings, X, from the newly elected government of the {Y}.'. Opens the parley.

nodes.label: ORE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has run out of {ore}, Your Excellency.  Our blacksmiths
nodes.trigger: During the colony turn update, the colony's ore stockpile is exhausted (ore over-production counter set this turn) while no consuming chain is present (blacksmiths can't get ore), so the 'out of ore' production report fires. Phase 8 of func_02D658.
nodes.inputs: Colony ore over-production counter set this turn plus a 'no blacksmith chain present' test; emitted in func_02D658 Phase 8.
nodes.outputs: Production warning: 'X has run out of ore, Your Excellency. Our blacksmiths cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'. (Note: this is a colony production report, not a Founding-Father event despite the worklist grouping.)

nodes.label: TOOLS
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has run out of {tools}, Your Excellency.  Our gunsmiths
nodes.trigger: During the colony turn update, the colony's tools stockpile is exhausted (tools over-production counter set) while no consuming chain is present (gunsmiths can't get tools). Phase 8 of func_02D658.
nodes.inputs: Colony tools over-production counter set this turn plus a 'no gunsmith chain present' test; emitted in func_02D658 Phase 8.
nodes.outputs: Production warning: 'X has run out of tools, Your Excellency. Our gunsmiths cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'. (Colony production report, not a Founding-Father event.)

nodes.label: ALREADYREVOLUTION
nodes.summary: We are already fighting a War of Independence, Excellency.
nodes.trigger: The player attempts to declare independence (request the King-audience / declare action) while the War of Independence is already in progress.
nodes.inputs: The revolution/war flag (already set).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We are already fighting a War of Independence, Excellency.' and takes no action.

nodes.label: APOSTATES
nodes.summary: "We note that you have signed a treaty with those unrepentant
nodes.trigger: European-power diplomacy meeting: a (Catholic) European power notes the player has signed a treaty with natives it considers heretics/unrepentant and demands (or requests) that the player cancel that treaty.
nodes.inputs: The meeting power and the native tribe in question; the request-vs-demand tone (MEEKNESS).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We note that you have signed a treaty with those unrepentant heretics, the X. We {request/demand} that you cancel this treaty at once' with 'Never! The X are our friends!' vs 'Yes! We shall crush the X together!'. The player's answer sets the diplomatic outcome.

nodes.label: BURNED
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} burn {%STRING3} to the ground!
nodes.trigger: In the deep tail of the land-combat decider, an attacking unit captures and razes a foreign/rebel colony (the player's own troops or the King's). The BURNED/BURNED2/BURNED3 verbs are chosen by the viewer/perspective (own colony razed vs spy report).
nodes.inputs: The attacking and defending units; the colony struct (loot/ownership); whether the target was a colony; the viewer power.
nodes.outputs: Captures/destroys the colony with the loot formula and shows 'X burn {colony} to the ground! Colonists flee in panic! King demands explanation!'.

nodes.label: CONSIDER
nodes.summary: %STRING0 is considering intervention on our behalf against the King,
nodes.trigger: During the War of Independence (revolution flag set, intervention-phase bits 2 and 4 clear), the per-turn Liberty-Bells tick for the active power makes its accumulated bells cross the threshold for the first time, unlocking the foreign-intervention offer. Fires once (then sets the intervention-considered phase bit).
nodes.inputs: Liberty bells produced this turn and the accumulated bells-toward-next; the revolution and intervention phase bits; the bells required for the next milestone; the intervening power.
nodes.outputs: Sets the intervention-considered phase bit (one-shot) and shows 'X is considering intervention on our behalf against the King... if we generate N liberty bells they will join us' (preceded by the AMBUSHHINT tip).

nodes.label: CONTINENTAL
nodes.summary: Our {Veteran %STRING0} have hardened to {Continental Army}
nodes.trigger: On-arrival unit-promotion check (the unit-arrive/reclassify routine): a Veteran unit hardens to Continental Army status. The revolution-gated branch requires the War of Independence flag set and the seceding-power flag.
nodes.inputs: The unit's type (soldier or dragoon eligible) and owner; the destination status/terrain value; the revolution flag and seceding-power flag; difficulty; the per-power active flag.
nodes.outputs: Reclassifies the unit to Continental Army status and shows 'Our Veteran {unit} have hardened to Continental Army status, Your Excellency!' (for a human, in-play European power).

nodes.label: DECLARE
nodes.summary: Shall we declare our independence from {%STRING0}, Your Excellency?
nodes.trigger: The player chooses the declare-independence action while national rebel sentiment is at least 50% (the majority gate) and the game is single-player. Presents the final confirmation.
nodes.inputs: National rebel sentiment % (>= 50 required, else TOOTORY); single-player vs multiplayer flag; the home power name.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Shall we declare our independence from X? This will end our turn and place us at war with our King!' with 'Never! That would be treasonous!' vs 'Yes! Give me liberty or give me death!'. Choosing yes runs the INDEPENDENCE handler.

nodes.label: DECLAREWAR
nodes.summary: The {%STRING0} and {%STRING1} are now at war.
nodes.trigger: Two powers go to war with each other (the right-click give-command / relation handler that sets the war relation between two powers). The largest function in this overlay (the AI unit evaluator) also hosts the rel-declare-war path.
nodes.inputs: The two powers' identities and their relation/treaty state.
nodes.outputs: Sets the war relation between the two named powers and shows 'The X and Y are now at war.'

nodes.label: EXPLOITS
nodes.summary: COLONIZATION RATING: %NUMBER0%%
nodes.trigger: End of game: the score/rank screen is displayed. The player's raw score is computed and mapped to a 0..23 rank title via a squared ladder clamped at 23, then this rating screen is rendered.
nodes.inputs: The player's raw power score (from the scoring function); the rank ladder; the player/leader name.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'COLONIZATION RATING: N%' and the rank-titled list of things named after the player ('the citizens give your name to...'); this is the end-of-game rating presentation.

nodes.label: FOREIGNNOTAVAIL
nodes.summary: The Foreign Affairs Adviser's report is no longer available
nodes.trigger: Player opens the Foreign Affairs Adviser report (F8) while the War of Independence flag is set. The handler's first act tests the revolution flag (bit 0) and bails if set.
nodes.inputs: The revolution/war-of-independence flag (global event flags, bit 0).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'The Foreign Affairs Adviser's report is no longer available once the War of Independence has begun' and returns without drawing the report.

nodes.label: FRIEND
nodes.summary: British General Cornwallis
nodes.trigger: Selector list of the intervening ally's general/admiral name strings (British General Cornwallis / French General Lafayette / Spanish Generals / Dutch Admiral de Ruyter), indexed by the intervening power. Used by the foreign-intervention routine to name the ally commander.
nodes.inputs: The intervening (ally) power index.
nodes.outputs: Provides the ally commander name string substituted into the INTERVENTION / INTERVENE announcements; not a standalone event message.

nodes.label: HOWTOWIN
nodes.summary: We have just won a glorious victory on the road to freedom, Your Excellency.
nodes.trigger: Shown after the rebels win a battle/colony during the War of Independence, explaining the victory conditions (the land-combat decider's revolution-progress message path).
nodes.inputs: The revolution state and the player's combat result.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We have just won a glorious victory on the road to freedom... to win our independence we must recapture all of our colonies from the King and destroy most of his ground forces in the New World.' (informational guidance).

nodes.label: INDEPENDENCE
nodes.summary: Continental Congress signs {Declaration of Independence}!
nodes.trigger: The player confirms the Declaration of Independence (after the DECLARE prompt). This handler sets up the war, flips the world into the revolution state, and announces it. It is the sole writer of the year-counter byte pair (century / year-of-century).
nodes.inputs: The seceding power and the current player; current year; the four powers' weighted scores (to pick the intervention ally); the ally's stat tables and difficulty (to size the REF + intervention force).
nodes.outputs: Sets the revolution flag (war declared); composes the REF and foreign-intervention force counts; transfers the player's tile-ownership to the ally; marks the current player at war; refreshes the seceding power's units; clears certain PowerRecord words; writes the year-counter pair; shows 'Continental Congress signs Declaration of Independence! ...Expeditionary force dispatched... General X calls for volunteers for the new Continental Army!'.

nodes.label: INTERVENE
nodes.summary: %STRING1 Intervention Force arrives in {%STRING0}!  Local Rebel Army
nodes.trigger: A foreign intervention force on the rebel side arrives next to one of the rebel power's coastal colonies (the AI/preview variant of the foreign-intervention landing, chosen by population-weighted colony pick).
nodes.inputs: The rebel/target power's coastal colonies and their populations; the intervening power's name id; the intervention-force composition counters; the chosen beach tile.
nodes.outputs: Spawns the intervention lead unit and stack at the chosen beach and shows 'X Intervention Force arrives in {colony}! Local Rebel Army commander regales X admiral'.

nodes.label: INTERVENTION
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} declares war on %STRING1 and joins the War of Independence
nodes.trigger: A foreign power formally declares war on the King and joins the War of Independence on the rebel side (the genuine intervention, as opposed to the preview/AI variant).
nodes.inputs: The intervening power and the King's power; the rebel target power; the intervention-force composition counters; the ally general/admiral name.
nodes.outputs: Decrements the intervention bookkeeping counters and shows 'X declares war on Y and joins the War of Independence on the Rebel side! ...navy plans bombardment of Tory-held fortifications'; spawns the lead intervention unit.

nodes.label: INVASION
nodes.summary: Royal Expeditionary Force lands near {%STRING0}!
nodes.trigger: Royal Expeditionary Force amphibious landing during the War of Independence: each turn the King's still-at-sea REF (Regulars/Cavalry/Men-o-War/Artillery counts) attempts to put land troops ashore next to one of the rebel power's coastal colonies. Gated on the REF Men-o-War count and total composition.
nodes.inputs: The REF composition counts (Regulars/Cavalry/Men-o-War/Artillery); the power's coastal colonies (those with the coastal/landable flag set), their Sons-of-Liberty %, population field, and garrison combat value; landing-tile capacity around each colony; difficulty.
nodes.outputs: Picks a colony (weighted by susceptibility and defense), pathfinds a beach tile, spawns the REF land stack (a royal land-unit type) there, plays the landing effects, shows 'Royal Expeditionary Force lands near X!', and decrements the committed REF counts.

nodes.label: KINGBUY
nodes.summary: King increases military spending.  {%STRING0} added to royal
nodes.trigger: The king increases military spending and adds a unit to the Royal Expeditionary Force (the REF-buildup path, run as the war/REF escalates).
nodes.inputs: The current REF composition; difficulty; the king's record.
nodes.outputs: Adds the named unit to the REF and shows 'King increases military spending. {unit} added to royal expeditionary force. Colonial leaders express alarm.' (no King sprite; a plain notification popup).

nodes.label: KINGLOSE
nodes.summary: "In our wisdom, we have decided to let you go
nodes.trigger: Endgame / end-of-war resolution in the per-turn king war handler: the player has won the War of Independence (the King concedes). Emitted as the King's final mocking concession cinematic line.
nodes.inputs: The revolution/war flag; the player's military and colony situation; the king/power records and the score-result accumulator.
nodes.outputs: Shows the King's concession speech ('In our wisdom, we have decided to let you go your own way...'); contributes to ending the war on the player's terms.

nodes.label: KINGLOWER
nodes.summary: "After careful consideration, we have graciously decided
nodes.trigger: The player asked the king to lower taxes and the king grants it: in the tax-change decision, the player declines the king's proposed raise, so the king instead lowers the rate by a small amount.
nodes.inputs: Current tax rate (king record); difficulty (sets the lower amount = roughly 5 minus difficulty); the random draw for the granted reduction.
nodes.outputs: Lowers the player's tax rate by the computed percentage and shows 'we have graciously decided to lower your tax rate by N%. The tax rate is now M%'.

nodes.label: KINGMOBILIZE
nodes.summary: Parliament votes additional funds to suppress
nodes.trigger: Parliament votes additional funds to suppress the revolution, mobilizing more royal forces in the rebel power's region.
nodes.inputs: The rebel power's region/colony being targeted; the REF composition; the king's record.
nodes.outputs: Mobilizes the named royal units in the target colony and shows 'Parliament votes additional funds to suppress revolution in X. {unit} mobilized in {colony}.' (no King sprite).

nodes.label: KINGNAVACT
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 %STRING1.  We are concerned that the Crown is not
nodes.trigger: The king imposes a Navigation Act as a reason for a tax raise (a flavored variant of the routine tax-raise event), citing that the Crown is not receiving its due share of New World revenue.
nodes.inputs: Current tax rate; difficulty/era-scaled raise amount; the king's record.
nodes.outputs: Raises the tax rate by the computed percentage and shows the Navigation-Act King's-audience message with the new rate, offering TAXOPTIONS (kiss ring / Tea Party).

nodes.label: KINGNEWWAR
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 %STRING1.  The arrogant attitude of the {%STRING2} has
nodes.trigger: The king declares a new war on a foreign power and orders the player to join it, cancelling the player's existing peace arrangement with that power.
nodes.inputs: The target foreign power; difficulty (sizes the gift gold and number of veteran soldiers); the king's record and the player's treasury.
nodes.outputs: Cancels the player's peace with the named power; grants the player gold from the Royal Treasury and a number of Veteran Soldier units; shows the declaration. Player may kiss the ring.

nodes.label: KINGRAISE
nodes.summary: "Your DARE to demand lower taxes!  After the kindness
nodes.trigger: Punitive tax raise: the player demanded lower taxes and, instead of granting it, the king raises taxes to punish the impudence (the 'yes/raise' branch of the king tax-change decision).
nodes.inputs: Current tax rate; difficulty/era-scaled raise amount (here doubled); the king's record.
nodes.outputs: Raises the tax rate by the computed percentage and shows 'You DARE to demand lower taxes!... we shall raise taxes by N%. The tax rate is now M%', offering TAXOPTIONS.

nodes.label: KINGSTAMPACT
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 %STRING1.  The ungrateful attitude of the colonists
nodes.trigger: The king imposes a Stamp Act on a named colony as a reason for a tax raise (flavored variant of the routine raise), citing the colonists' ungrateful attitude.
nodes.inputs: Current tax rate; difficulty/era-scaled raise amount; the colony named in the message; the king's record.
nodes.outputs: Raises the tax rate by the computed percentage and shows the Stamp-Act King's-audience message with the new rate, offering TAXOPTIONS.

nodes.label: KINGTAX
nodes.summary: "It is essential that the Crown receive proper
nodes.trigger: The king's routine tax-raise event fires (a Navigation-Act-style raise). The king periodically decides to raise the player's tax rate; the proposed increase is computed and applied, then this audience message announces it.
nodes.inputs: Current tax rate (king record); difficulty (sets the base increment) and turn/era (era multiplier); the king's record.
nodes.outputs: Raises the player's tax rate by the computed percentage and shows the King's-audience message stating the increase and the new rate, offering the TAXOPTIONS choice (kiss the ring or hold a Tea Party).

nodes.label: KINGVICTORY
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 %STRING1.  To celebrate our recent victory
nodes.trigger: The king's forces win a battle in one of the King's wars, so the king magnanimously lowers the player's tax rate to celebrate the victory.
nodes.inputs: Current tax rate; the lower amount; the enemy power named in the message; the king's record.
nodes.outputs: Lowers the player's tax rate by the computed percentage and shows 'To celebrate our recent victory over X, we have decided to LOWER your tax rate by N%. The tax rate is now M%'.

nodes.label: KINGWAR
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 %STRING1.  Because of recent developments in our
