nodes.trigger: An ongoing King's war continues, which the king uses as justification to raise the player's tax rate.
nodes.inputs: Current tax rate; difficulty/era-scaled raise amount; the enemy power named in the message; the king's record.
nodes.outputs: Raises the tax rate by the computed percentage and shows 'Because of recent developments in our ongoing war with X, we have decided to raise your tax rate by N%...', offering TAXOPTIONS.

nodes.label: KINGWIFE
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 %STRING1.  In honor of our recent wedding to
nodes.trigger: Random king's-wedding event: in honor of the king's recent marriage, the king raises the player's tax rate.
nodes.inputs: Current tax rate; difficulty/era-scaled raise amount; the king's record.
nodes.outputs: Raises the tax rate by the computed percentage and shows 'In honor of our recent wedding to our X wife, we have decided to raise your tax rate by N%...', offering TAXOPTIONS.

nodes.label: KINGWIN
nodes.summary: "As expected, your attempt to separate from
nodes.trigger: Endgame / end-of-war resolution in the per-turn king war handler: the King's Royal forces have defeated the rebellion (player loses the War of Independence).
nodes.inputs: The revolution/war flag; the player's military/colony situation; the king/power records.
nodes.outputs: Shows the King's triumphant speech ('your attempt to separate from mother X has proven futile... Rag Tag armies are no match for our Royal forces'); the player loses the war.

nodes.label: KISSUP
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} is currently under Parliamentary {boycott}, Your Excellency.
nodes.trigger: Player clicks a boycotted cargo type (on the Europe screen) to request that Parliament lift the boycott. For a human-controlled, in-play power, this confirm-and-pay dialog is shown asking for the accumulated back taxes.
nodes.inputs: The boycotted commodity; the back-tax cost (a per-unit fee scaled by quantity); the power's treasury gold; the per-unit 'owes payment' bitmask.
nodes.outputs: Offers 'Pay N gold' vs refuse. On accept and sufficient gold: deducts the back taxes from the treasury, adds them to cumulative spend, clears that commodity's boycott bit (lifting the boycott). If gold is short it falls through to the KISSSORRY 'we only have N available' message.

nodes.label: LANDFIRST
nodes.summary: Land units cannot enter an enemy occupied square
nodes.trigger: A land unit aboard a ship tries to move directly into an enemy-occupied square from the ship. The ship move/arrival handler's destination classifier disallows it (the enemy-occupied destination code).
nodes.inputs: The mover's type (a land unit aboard a ship), the destination tile's owner/occupant and terrain.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Land units cannot enter an enemy occupied square from on board a ship. You must first unload them into an empty or friendly-occupied square.' and aborts the move.

nodes.label: LOOTCASH
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} treasure fleet laden with {%NUMBER0$} arrives safely in %STRING1!
nodes.trigger: A treasure (from looting a native settlement or a lost city) is transported home: the King's galleon ferries the player's treasure fleet safely to Europe, and the Crown takes a tax-rate share. (Verified emitter is the treasure-transport event func_05C878; the worklist's func_041EEA is the per-turn unit-order/supply driver and does not push this string.)
nodes.inputs: The settlement/treasure source size; the attacker power record (gold, total-loot, score fields); the current tax rate (Crown's share); the home-port name.
nodes.outputs: Adds the player's share to the treasury (and the Crown-share remainder to loot/score totals) and shows 'X treasure fleet laden with N gold arrives safely in {port}! Crown takes M% share. Z added to treasury.'

nodes.label: LOOTFOREIGN
nodes.summary: Spies report: {%STRING0} treasure fleet laden with {%NUMBER0$} arrives
nodes.trigger: Spy report when a FOREIGN power's treasure fleet arrives in its home port (the foreign-power equivalent of LOOTCASH), reported during that power's unit move/turn processing.
nodes.inputs: The foreign power's treasure amount and home port; the foreign king's reaction.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Spies report: X treasure fleet laden with N gold arrives in {port}. X king pleased with booty.' (informational only).

nodes.label: MERCENARIES
nodes.summary: The King of %STRING0 has offered to send us a force of trained {mercenaries}
nodes.trigger: Wartime foreign-mercenary offer: 1-in-3 chance per applicable turn (suppressed while a foreign intervention is pending) for a foreign king to offer the player a force of trained mercenaries for gold, when the price is within the player's treasury.
nodes.inputs: Difficulty (sizes package and price); random draws for package size, category, and price; the offering power name; the player's treasury gold.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'The King of X has offered to send us a force of trained mercenaries (units) in exchange for N gold' with 'Pay N' vs 'No thank you'. On accept and affordable, debits the treasury and applies the purchase (the bought force is later landed by the MERCS path).

nodes.label: MERCENARY
nodes.summary: The {%STRING0} declare war on the {%STRING1}.
nodes.trigger: European-power diplomacy SMITE branch: after the player pays a European power to attack (smite) another power, that paid power declares war on the target.
nodes.inputs: The two powers involved (the paid power and the target); the war-relation matrix.
nodes.outputs: Sets the war relation (sets the at-war bit) and shows 'The X declare war on the Y.'

nodes.label: MERCS
nodes.summary: %STRING1 mercenaries arrive in %STRING0.
nodes.trigger: Mercenaries the player purchased (from a foreign king's mercenary offer) arrive: handled by the same foreign-landing routine (the variant path), placing the bought force near a coastal colony.
nodes.inputs: The target power's coastal colonies; the offering power's name id; the force composition counts; the chosen beach tile.
nodes.outputs: Spawns the mercenary stack near the colony and shows 'X mercenaries arrive in {colony}'.

nodes.label: MOBILIZE
nodes.summary: Continental Army mobilizes at {%STRING0}! Our Veteran %STRING1
nodes.trigger: After a Sons-of-Liberty surge: for a colony of the rebel power whose Sons-of-Liberty % is at least 50%, exactly one garrisoned 'rebel' veteran unit (marked by the rebel-variant flag) is converted to Continental Army (the veteran-soldier type is promoted to the Continental-soldier type).
nodes.inputs: The colony's owner power and Sons-of-Liberty %; the colony's population field; the garrisoned units' types and rebel-variant flag.
nodes.outputs: Promotes the veteran unit's type to Continental Army; applies a terrain change and shows 'Continental Army mobilizes at {colony}! Our Veteran {unit} have been promoted to Continental Army status.'

nodes.label: MOBILIZE2
nodes.summary: Continental Army mobilizes at {%STRING0}! {%NUMBER0} Veteran
nodes.trigger: Same Sons-of-Liberty-surge conversion as MOBILIZE, but more than one garrisoned rebel veteran unit is converted in the colony (veteran soldiers and veteran dragoons promoted to their Continental-Army equivalents), up to a clamp of (population/2)*(SoL%-50)/50.
nodes.inputs: The colony's owner power and Sons-of-Liberty %; the colony's population field; the garrisoned units' types and rebel-variant flag; the count converted.
nodes.outputs: Promotes that many veteran units to Continental Army; applies a terrain change and shows 'Continental Army mobilizes at {colony}! {N} Veteran units have been promoted to Continental Army status.'

nodes.label: MULTIREV
nodes.summary: ^^Warning!
nodes.trigger: The player attempts to declare independence in a multiplayer game (the auto-revolution events are disabled in multiplayer).
nodes.inputs: The multiplayer flag.
nodes.outputs: Shows the warning 'The Revolution does not function in multi-player mode. If you declare independence, the game will become a single player game. Are you sure?' with 'Declare independence' vs 'Never Mind'; declaring converts the game to single-player.

nodes.label: NOCOLONIESEITHER
nodes.summary: New colonies cannot be founded during the {War of Independence}.
nodes.trigger: Player presses Build-Colony (B) with the active unit while the War of Independence flag is set (the global revolution flag, bit 0). The gate is checked before any other colony-validity test.
nodes.inputs: The revolution/war-of-independence flag (global event flags, bit 0); the active unit.
nodes.outputs: Shows the message 'New colonies cannot be founded during the War of Independence' and aborts the build command; no colony is created.

nodes.label: NOMAYORSDURINGREV
nodes.summary: Scouts cannot meet with mayors during the {War of Independence}.
nodes.trigger: A scout tries to 'Meet With Mayor' at a colony while the War of Independence is active. (The assigned func_059B90 is the AI unit-target evaluator, which does not push this string; the actual guard is in the scout-meeting action and keys off the revolution flag.)
nodes.inputs: The revolution/war-of-independence flag.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Scouts cannot meet with mayors during the War of Independence.' and blocks the scout's meet-mayor action.

nodes.label: OTHERLESS
nodes.summary: Spies Report:  Only {%NUMBER0} {%STRING1} now support independence
nodes.trigger: Per-turn king/war handler spy-report path: a foreign European power that was approaching its own independence loses popular support, so the count of its colonists favoring liberty has dropped.
nodes.inputs: The other power's colonist-support-for-independence count vs the threshold required; the friend/support ratio between the powers.
nodes.outputs: Shows the 'Spies Report: Only N support independence from X. The King will not grant liberty unless M are in favor' message; no state change for the player.

nodes.label: OTHERMIGHT
nodes.summary: Your Excellency, the King of {%STRING0} is considering granting independence
nodes.trigger: Per-turn king/war handler: a foreign European power is nearing independence for its own colonies (enough of its colonists support liberty that the King is considering granting it).
nodes.inputs: The other power's colonists-supporting-independence count, its total colonists, and the threshold needed; the per-power friend/support ratio.
nodes.outputs: Shows the 'the King of X is considering granting independence... once M colonists support liberty, the X colonies will be granted freedom' advisory; no direct player-state change.

nodes.label: REBELDOWN
nodes.summary: {Tory} sentiment is once again on the rise in the colonies, Your
nodes.trigger: Pre-revolution: at the per-turn national recompute, rebel sentiment falls into a lower ten-point band ((%+4)/10 below the previously latched band) for the active/rebel power (with at least 4 colonies).
nodes.inputs: Recomputed national rebel sentiment %; the previous band latch.
nodes.outputs: Latches the new lower band and shows the 'Tory sentiment is once again on the rise... only N% support independence' message.

nodes.label: REBELMAJORITY
nodes.summary: Sons of Liberty membership in {%STRING0} is up to %NUMBER0%%, Your
nodes.trigger: During a colony's end-of-turn Sons-of-Liberty settlement, the colony's rebel sentiment (its Sons-of-Liberty membership %) reaches at least 50% and the colony was not already latched into the rebel-majority band (colony flags bit 4 clear).
nodes.inputs: The colony's rebel sentiment % (computed from its Liberty Bells vs population); the colony's owner power; the colony's band-latch flags.
nodes.outputs: Sets the colony's rebel-majority latch (flags bit 4); every colonist in that colony gains a +1 bonus to base production. Shows the 'Sons of Liberty membership is up to N%... A majority support independence' message.

nodes.label: REBELUNANIMOUS
nodes.summary: Sons of Liberty membership in {%STRING0} is up to 100%%, Your Excellency.
nodes.trigger: A colony's rebel sentiment reaches 100% (full Sons-of-Liberty membership) and the colony was not already latched into the unanimous band (colony flags bit 2 clear).
nodes.inputs: The colony's rebel sentiment %; the colony's owner power; the unanimous-band latch flag.
nodes.outputs: Sets the unanimous latch (flags bit 2); colonists gain a +2 production bonus and can be educated more quickly. Shows the 'membership is up to 100%... +2 to base production' message.

nodes.label: REBELUP
nodes.summary: {Rebel} sentiment is rising in the colonies, Your Excellency!
nodes.trigger: Pre-revolution only: at the active/rebel power's end-of-turn Sons-of-Liberty recompute, national rebel sentiment rises into a new ten-point band (current %/10 greater than the previously latched band), while national % is still below 50%. Gated to powers with at least 4 colonies.
nodes.inputs: Recomputed national rebel sentiment %; the previous ten-point band latch; the power's colony count.
nodes.outputs: Latches the new ten-point band and shows the 'Rebel sentiment is rising... N% support independence... any colony with 50% Sons of Liberty gets +1' message.

nodes.label: REBELUP50
nodes.summary: {Rebel} sentiment is rising in the colonies, Your Excellency!
nodes.trigger: Pre-revolution: same per-turn national rebel-sentiment recompute as REBELUP, but national sentiment has now risen into a new band that is at or above 50%. The first time a power crosses 50% with no rebel power yet designated, that power is marked as the rebel (future USA) power.
nodes.inputs: Recomputed national rebel sentiment %; the previous band latch; whether a rebel power has been designated yet.
nodes.outputs: Marks this power as the rebel power (enabling the Declare-Independence option). Shows the 'N% support independence... Founding Fathers think we should declare independence' message.

nodes.label: SCREWED
nodes.summary: "These are the burial grounds of our
nodes.trigger: Lost-City-Rumour engine, burial-mounds outcome (the player chose to search ancient burial mounds): if the exploring player is human and the tribe turns hostile, the SCREWED key is appended after the BURIAL result.
nodes.inputs: Whether the explorer is the human player; the burial-mounds outcome roll; the tribe whose sacred ground was disturbed.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'These are the burial grounds of our ancient X fathers! You have trespassed on sacred land. Now you must die!' and the natives turn hostile / attack the expedition.

nodes.label: SEIZURE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} seized on the high seas by the Royal Navy!
nodes.trigger: Per-power scan (over all units owned by a given power) for that power's land/transport units (the land-unit type range) standing on a tile that is off the active on-screen view; the King's Royal Navy seizes such off-screen shipping/goods.
nodes.inputs: The unit count and UnitRecord table; per-unit owner and type; whether each unit's tile is on the active view.
nodes.outputs: Sets the per-type message argument and shows '{cargo} seized on the high seas by the Royal Navy!' for each qualifying unit, then refreshes that unit slot.

nodes.label: SEIZURELAND
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} captured by the Royal Army!
nodes.trigger: At a given map tile, the scan finds a FOREIGN European land unit (owner not the current player, owner is one of the four European powers, that power still in play) of a land-unit type, and the tile-has-target test fails for that unit (a land seizure context).
nodes.inputs: The target tile coordinates; the unit's owner, type, and per-power flag; the tile-has-target test.
nodes.outputs: Sets the per-type message argument and shows '{unit/cargo} captured by the Royal Army!', then refreshes the unit slot.

nodes.label: SEIZURESEA
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} captured at sea by the Royal Navy!
nodes.trigger: Same per-tile foreign-land-unit scan as SEIZURELAND, but on the sea-capture branch (the tile-has-target test passes and the unit is a qualifying land-unit type being captured at sea by the Royal Navy).
nodes.inputs: The target tile coordinates; the unit's owner, type, and per-power flag; the tile-has-target test.
nodes.outputs: Sets the per-type message argument and shows '{unit/cargo} captured at sea by the Royal Navy!', then refreshes the unit slot.

nodes.label: SOMEBOYCOTT
nodes.summary: Some of the cargo could not be unloaded because of a parliamentary
nodes.trigger: On the Europe screen, the player tries to unload cargo from a ship into the home port but one or more of the cargo types are under a Parliamentary boycott (imposed by an earlier Tea Party), so that cargo cannot be sold.
nodes.inputs: The ship's cargo types vs the per-power boycott bitmap (which goods Parliament has boycotted).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Some of the cargo could not be unloaded because of a parliamentary boycott...' and leaves the boycotted cargo on the ship; clicking the boycotted cargo type opens the back-tax (KISSUP) lift-boycott dialog.

nodes.label: SUCCESSION
nodes.summary: War of the Spanish Succession ends in Europe!
nodes.trigger: Single-player War-of-the-Spanish-Succession event: the four European powers are ranked by a weighted score; the strongest still-eligible crown (winner) annexes the weakest still-eligible crown (loser). Early-out if a particular global status bit is already set.
nodes.inputs: Per-power weighted score tables; per-power defeat flags; map ownership/visibility layers; the loser's units, colonies, and native-mission records.
nodes.outputs: Transfers all of the loser's tile ownership/visibility, units, colonies (reassigning owner, clearing siege fields), and missions to the winner; marks the loser defeated; makes the loser the active player and redraws. Shows the 'War of the Spanish Succession ends... cede X to the winner... Treaty of Utrecht' message.

nodes.label: TAXOPTIONS
nodes.summary: Kiss pinky ring.
nodes.trigger: Appended as the response options to every tax-RAISE King's-audience message (KINGTAX/KINGRAISE/KINGNAVACT/KINGSTAMPACT/KINGWAR/KINGWIFE/MERCANTILISM/PURCHASETAX). It is a combine-options target the dispatcher concatenates onto the raise message.
nodes.inputs: The boycottable commodity name (used to label the 'X Party' option).
nodes.outputs: Presents two choices: 'Kiss pinky ring' (accept the new tax) or 'Hold a {commodity} Party' (refuse the tax and trigger a Tea Party / TEAPARTY for that commodity).

nodes.label: TEAPARTY
nodes.summary: {%STRING3 Party}!  Sons of Liberty throw {%NUMBER0} tons of %STRING0
nodes.trigger: The player chose 'Hold a {commodity} Party' from the TAXOPTIONS prompt instead of paying the new tax.
nodes.inputs: The commodity chosen for the party; the colony where it is held; the quantity of that commodity thrown into the sea; the home-port name.
nodes.outputs: The Sons of Liberty dump that commodity's stores into the sea; the new tax is refused; Parliament announces a boycott of that commodity (sets the boycott bit so it cannot be traded in Europe until lifted). Also increments the king's anger counter. Shows the Tea Party message.

nodes.label: TOOTORY
nodes.summary: Only {%NUMBER0%%} of the colonists support the independence
nodes.trigger: The player tries to declare independence but national rebel sentiment is below 50% (no majority behind the independence movement).
nodes.inputs: National rebel sentiment %.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Only N% of the colonists support the independence movement... We cannot start a rebellion against the King until the majority is behind us.' and blocks the declaration.

nodes.label: TORYMAJORITY
nodes.summary: Sons of Liberty membership in {%STRING0} is down to %NUMBER0%%, Your
nodes.trigger: A colony that was in the rebel-majority band (majority latch bit 4 set) sees rebel sentiment fall below 50%.
nodes.inputs: The colony's rebel sentiment %; the majority-band latch flag.
nodes.outputs: Clears the majority latch; the colony loses its production bonus entirely. Shows the 'membership is down to N%... no longer gain production bonuses' message.

nodes.label: TORYMINORITY
nodes.summary: Sons of Liberty membership in {%STRING0} is down from 100%% to %NUMBER0%%,
nodes.trigger: A colony that was previously at unanimous (100%) Sons-of-Liberty support (unanimous latch bit 2 set) sees rebel sentiment fall below 95%.
nodes.inputs: The colony's rebel sentiment %; the unanimous-band latch flag.
nodes.outputs: Drops the colony out of the unanimous band; its production bonus is reduced from +2 back to +1. Shows the 'membership is down from 100% to N%... only +1 to base production' message.

nodes.label: TORYUPRISING
nodes.summary: Tory uprising near %STRING0!  Parliament arms Tory Militia!
nodes.trigger: Random hostile-spawn event against one colony of a given power. An opening roll (random_int over 0..difficulty+1) must succeed; then the most susceptible eligible colony is chosen by a score = colony field x ((100 - Sons-of-Liberty %) x 2)/100 + difficulty + 1, minus garrison defense, and suppressed if a current-player unit is adjacent.
nodes.inputs: Difficulty; per-colony susceptibility field, Sons-of-Liberty %, garrison defense (def table per unit type); adjacency of current-player units; the colony's surrounding work tiles.
nodes.outputs: Flags the chosen colony and spawns Tory-militia hostile units on its open work tiles (with a chance of upgrading their type/variant per severity step); applies a terrain change and shows 'Tory uprising near X! Parliament arms Tory Militia!'. If nothing spawned, clears the colony flag.

nodes.label: TRADEWITH
nodes.summary: "We will give you {%NUMBER0 %STRING0} in exchange for your %NUMBER1 %STRING1.
nodes.trigger: A native village offers the player a goods-for-goods (or goods-for-gold) trade in the native trade dialog. (The assigned func_05A40E is the foreign-EUROPEAN-power trade dialog, which pushes TRADEATWAR/TRADEMERCANTILISM/TRADENOCARGO/TRADEWHICH but not TRADEWITH; the actual emitter is the native trade handler.)
nodes.inputs: The cargo the player carries and the cargo the village offers in return; the gold-equivalent offer; the village's wants.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We will give you N X in exchange for your M Y. Or, if you like, we are willing to give you Z gold. Is this satisfactory?' with options to take the goods, take the gold, or refuse; the chosen option performs the exchange.

nodes.label: ALREADYSMITE
nodes.summary: "We are already at war with the worthless {%STRING0}."
nodes.trigger: Player asks a European power (in diplomacy) to attack a native tribe they are already at war with.
nodes.inputs: The named tribe and the other power's existing war state against it.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We are already at war with the worthless {tribe}.'

nodes.label: BADHAGGLE0
nodes.summary: "Our patience with your haggling is exhausted.
nodes.trigger: While trading goods with a native village, the player haggles too long and the natives lose patience with this offer.
nodes.inputs: The cargo being offered to the natives.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Our patience with your haggling is exhausted. We no longer want your worthless {cargo}...' and ends this trade.

nodes.label: BADHAGGLE1
nodes.summary: "We have already told you that we no longer want your
nodes.trigger: Player returns to trade the same cargo the natives already refused after over-haggling.
nodes.inputs: The previously refused cargo.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We have already told you that we no longer want your {cargo}. Come back when you have something else.'

nodes.label: BRING
nodes.summary: "We are in need of {%STRING0} and {%STRING1}.  Perhaps you will
nodes.trigger: After a native trade interaction, the village hints at what goods it wants for next time.
nodes.inputs: The two/three cargo types the village is in need of.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We are in need of {A} and {B}. Perhaps you will bring some next time... Even {C} would be of some value.'

nodes.label: BUYME0
nodes.summary: Cost to complete %STRING0: %NUMBER0$.
nodes.trigger: Player asks to rush/complete a colony's current build project but cannot afford it (information-only variant, no choices).
nodes.inputs: The current build item's name, the gold cost to complete it, and the treasury balance.
nodes.outputs: Displays 'Cost to complete X: $N. Treasury: $M.' as an informational message (no buy option offered because funds are insufficient).

nodes.label: BUYME1
nodes.summary: Cost to complete %STRING0: %NUMBER0$.
nodes.trigger: Player asks to rush/complete a colony's current build project and can afford it (choice variant).
nodes.inputs: The current build item's name, the gold cost to complete it, and the treasury balance.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Cost to complete X: $N. Treasury: $M.' with options Never mind / Complete it; choosing Complete spends the gold and finishes the build.

nodes.label: CANCELPEACE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} cancel peace treaty with {%STRING1}.
nodes.trigger: A peace treaty between two powers is cancelled (e.g. via the right-click give-command / declare-war handler, or when a power breaks a treaty).
nodes.inputs: The two power/tribe names whose treaty is ending.
nodes.outputs: Announces '{power} cancel peace treaty with {power}.' and sets the two parties' relations to no-treaty/war.

nodes.label: CANESUGAR
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has run out of {sugar}, Your Excellency.  Our distillers
nodes.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored sugar so its distillers cannot work.
nodes.inputs: The colony's sugar stock (zero) and the colony name.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of sugar... Our distillers cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

nodes.label: COTTON
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has run out of {cotton}, Your Excellency.  Our weavers
nodes.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored cotton so its weavers cannot work.
nodes.inputs: The colony's cotton stock (zero) and the colony name.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of cotton... Our weavers cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

nodes.label: DEPLETION
nodes.summary: Mine depleted near %STRING0.
nodes.trigger: During colony turn processing, a worked resource tile in the colony's surrounding ring (a mine/ore site) becomes depleted.
nodes.inputs: Sweep of the colony's 8 surrounding cells, each cell's terrain class (resource-bearing 6/7) and feature; the colony name.
nodes.outputs: Changes the depleted map tile and shows 'Mine depleted near {colony}.'

nodes.label: EVASIVE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0 %STRING1} evades {%STRING2 %STRING3}.
nodes.trigger: In combat, an attacking unit's strike misses and the defender evades it (combat-outcome verb emitted by the land-combat decider).
nodes.inputs: Attacker and defender unit names/owners, the resolved combat roll.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{attacker} evades {defender}.' (an inconsequential / dodged engagement).

nodes.label: EXTORTNO
nodes.summary: "You must think us very foolish indeed, %STRING0 %STRING1.  The {%STRING2}
nodes.trigger: A scout/unit demands tribute (extortion) from a native village but the village refuses outright.
nodes.inputs: The player's leader title and the tribe identity.
nodes.outputs: Shows the refusal 'You must think us very foolish indeed... The {tribe} will not be taken in by your tricks and treachery.'

nodes.label: EXTORTPOOR
nodes.summary: "Mighty %STRING0, we tremble before you.  Alas, the humble and
nodes.trigger: A unit extorts a native village that has no goods worth giving.
nodes.inputs: The player's leader title and the tribe identity.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'the humble and peaceloving {tribe} have no gifts worthy of your magnificence. We pray that you will be merciful and spare us.'

nodes.label: EXTORTSTUFF
nodes.summary: "Great %STRING0, we bow before the might of your strange weapons.
nodes.trigger: A unit successfully extorts goods from an intimidated native village.
nodes.inputs: The player's leader title, the tribe, the goods amount/type extorted, and the destination colony.
nodes.outputs: Shows the village conceding to deliver {N} {goods} to {colony} to be spared, and the goods are transferred.

nodes.label: FURS
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has run out of {furs}, Your Excellency.  Our fur traders
nodes.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored furs so its fur traders cannot work.
nodes.inputs: The colony's furs stock (zero) and the colony name.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of furs... Our fur traders cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

nodes.label: GIFTS
nodes.summary: "We present you with a gift of {%NUMBER0$} in exchange for
nodes.trigger: During a European-power diplomacy meeting the other power offers a gift of gold for continued forbearance.
nodes.inputs: The gift amount in gold.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We present you with a gift of $N in exchange for your continued forbearance.' and credits the gold.

nodes.label: HAVETREATY
nodes.summary: "We have signed a peace treaty with the {%STRING0},
nodes.trigger: The active unit tries to build a colony or act on a tile adjacent to a native settlement of a tribe with whom you have a peace treaty.
nodes.inputs: The active unit, an 8-neighbour scan for an adjacent native settlement owned by a matching tribe, the tribe identity.
nodes.outputs: Warns 'We have signed a peace treaty with the {tribe}' and offers Cancel Action or Break Treaty; breaking the treaty flags the settlement and claims the tile.

nodes.label: KISSSORRY
nodes.summary: Unfortunately, we only have {%NUMBER0$} available.
nodes.trigger: Player agrees to pay back-taxes to lift a Parliamentary boycott (after the KISSUP prompt) but does not have enough gold.
nodes.inputs: The player's available gold (less than the back-tax amount demanded).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Unfortunately, we only have $N available.' and the boycott is not lifted.

nodes.label: LEARNSTAY
nodes.summary: "You are unskilled, Young One, and your ways are
nodes.trigger: An unskilled colonist (Young One) visits a native village willing to teach him a master profession.
nodes.inputs: The tribe and the master profession they can teach.
nodes.outputs: Offers 'we {tribe} will show you how to become a master {profession}' with choices to become the master now or decline.

nodes.label: LUMBER
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has run out of {lumber}, Your Excellency.  Our carpenters
nodes.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored lumber so its carpenters cannot work.
nodes.inputs: The colony's lumber stock (zero) and the colony name.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of lumber... Our carpenters cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

nodes.label: NEEDTOOLS
nodes.summary: {%STRING1} under construction in {%STRING0} requires
nodes.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony's build project needs more tools than are available to finish.
nodes.inputs: The colony name, the building under construction, the tools required for completion, and the tools currently available.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{building} under construction in {colony} requires {N} tools for completion. Only {M} tools are currently available.'

nodes.label: NOCONTACT
nodes.summary: "We have no contact with the {%STRING0}."
nodes.trigger: Player asks a power to act against a tribe with whom that power has had no contact.
nodes.inputs: The named tribe and the asked power's contact state.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We have no contact with the {tribe}.'

nodes.label: NOTENOUGH
nodes.summary: "Sadly, your treasury ({%NUMBER0$}) is not large enough to
nodes.trigger: During a native trade the player promises a buy/payment larger than their treasury can back.
nodes.inputs: The player's treasury balance.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Sadly, your treasury ($N) is not large enough to back your promise.' and the deal falls through.

nodes.label: ORDINAL
nodes.summary: first
nodes.trigger: Not a dialog: an ordinal-word lookup table (first, second, third, ... thirtieth) used to compose other messages.
nodes.inputs: A 1-based index into the ordinal list.
nodes.outputs: Returns the ordinal word for that index (e.g. for naming the Nth founding father, Nth wife, etc.) to be inserted into another message.

nodes.label: PEACEUSA
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} welcomes peace with our politically backward neighbors,
nodes.trigger: In diplomacy with an independent (post-revolution USA) nation, that nation responds to a peace proposal.
nodes.inputs: The USA nation name and your nation name.
nodes.outputs: Shows the USA peace response with reply options (Go in peace / withdraw forces first / threat / suggest an alliance).

nodes.label: PROVOKE
nodes.summary: "We can no longer tolerate your foul provocations.  Prepare for WAR!"
nodes.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting the other power declares war over your provocations.
nodes.inputs: The meeting context (accumulated provocations/attitude).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We can no longer tolerate your foul provocations. Prepare for WAR!' and sets the two powers at war.

nodes.label: REFIT
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has completed its repairs in {%STRING1}.
nodes.trigger: A damaged ship that had returned to a colony/Europe for repairs finishes repairing.
nodes.inputs: The ship's name and the port/colony where it was repaired.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{ship} has completed its repairs in {port}.'

nodes.label: RID
nodes.summary: "In the name of {%STRING0}, we order you to leave {%STRING1} immediately.
nodes.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting the other power orders you to leave a region/the hemisphere or be driven out.
nodes.inputs: The power's sponsor name and the region/colony in question.
nodes.outputs: Shows the ultimatum 'we order you to leave {region} immediately. If you do not, we shall drive you into the sea.'

nodes.label: SIGNTREATY
nodes.summary: The {%STRING0} and {%STRING1} have signed a peace treaty.
nodes.trigger: Two powers/tribes conclude a peace treaty (announcement).
nodes.inputs: The two party names.
nodes.outputs: Announces 'The {A} and {B} have signed a peace treaty.'

nodes.label: THREATS
nodes.summary: "We laugh at your feeble threats."
nodes.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting the other power dismisses your threat.
nodes.inputs: The meeting context.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We laugh at your feeble threats.'

nodes.label: TOBACCO
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} has run out of {tobacco}, Your Excellency.  Our tobacconists
nodes.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored tobacco so its tobacconists cannot work.
nodes.inputs: The colony's tobacco stock (zero) and the colony name.
nodes.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of tobacco... Our tobacconists cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

nodes.label: TRADEDELETE
nodes.summary: Which trade route should we {delete}:
nodes.trigger: Player chooses to delete a defined trade route.
nodes.inputs: The list of existing trade routes (route count) and the chosen route to delete.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Which trade route should we delete:' then, on confirmation, detaches units assigned to it, compacts the route table, and decrements the route count.

nodes.label: TRADENONE
nodes.summary: You have not yet defined any trade routes.
nodes.trigger: Player tries to assign a unit to a trade route but no trade routes have been defined yet.
nodes.inputs: The trade-route count (zero).
nodes.outputs: Shows 'You have not yet defined any trade routes.' and aborts the assignment.

nodes.label: TRADENOWANT
nodes.summary: "We are not interested in your {%NUMBER0 %STRING0}.  Come back when
nodes.trigger: A wagon train / ship offers goods to a native village that is not interested in that cargo.
nodes.inputs: The offered cargo amount and type.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'We are not interested in your {N} {cargo}. Come back when you have something better to offer.'

nodes.label: TRADESELECT
nodes.summary: Select a trade route:
nodes.trigger: Player assigns a unit to a trade route and at least one route exists, opening the route picker.
nodes.inputs: The active unit, its type (ship vs land determines route kind), and the list of defined trade routes.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Select a trade route:'; on a pick the unit is assigned to that route and put into trade-route order.

nodes.label: UNFORTUNATE
nodes.summary: "Unfortunately, your treasury is insufficient to
nodes.trigger: Player agrees to pay a power (e.g. to smite a tribe or move forces) but lacks the gold to cover the promise.
nodes.inputs: The player's treasury balance versus the promised amount.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'Unfortunately, your treasury is insufficient to match your extravagant promises.' and the deal is void.

nodes.label: WARMANLY
nodes.summary: "You reject our generous offer?  Then in the name of
nodes.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting you reject a power's offer and it declares war (the assertive 'manly' variant).
nodes.inputs: The power's sponsor name and the region in question.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'You reject our generous offer? Then in the name of {sponsor} we shall wipe you from the face of the New World. Prepare for WAR!'

nodes.label: WITHDRAW
nodes.summary: "In the interest of peace, we shall withdraw our forces."
nodes.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting the other power agrees to withdraw its forces in the interest of peace.
nodes.inputs: The withdraw-negotiation outcome.
nodes.outputs: Shows 'In the interest of peace, we shall withdraw our forces.' and the forces pull back to Europe.

nodes.label: CHIEFAREA
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} are pleased to welcome travelers
nodes.trigger: Fires when a Scout enters a native settlement and the village offers tales of nearby lands: a positive 'speak with the chief' outcome that reveals surrounding terrain.
nodes.inputs: The visiting Scout unit and the settlement's tribe; a random visit-outcome roll modified by Scout/Seasoned-Scout status and tribe attitude.
nodes.outputs: The chief welcomes the travelers and reveals/explores the nearby map ("...Come sit by the fire and we shall tell you tales of nearby lands."); the surrounding tiles around the settlement are uncovered for the player.

nodes.label: CHIEFBORED
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} are always pleased to welcome {%STRING1}
nodes.trigger: Fires when a Scout re-enters a native settlement that has already been visited / has nothing more to offer: a neutral 'nothing new here' outcome.
nodes.inputs: The visiting unit and the settlement (already-visited / exhausted state); the tribe.
nodes.outputs: The village gives a polite, empty greeting with no reward ("The {tribe} are always pleased to welcome {nationality} travelers."); the visit ends with no gold/guides/tales.

nodes.label: CHIEFGIFT
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} welcome the emissaries of the {%STRING1}
nodes.trigger: Fires when a Scout enters a native settlement and the village's 'speak with the chief' outcome is a gift of beads/gold (treasure offering).
nodes.inputs: The visiting Scout and the settlement's tribe; a random outcome roll (Scout/Seasoned-Scout improves results); a gift-value roll.
nodes.outputs: The village gives the player a gift worth a stated sum of gold ("Please take these valuable beads (worth {amount}) back to your chieftain..."); that gold is credited to the player's treasury.

nodes.label: CHIEFGUIDES
nodes.summary: "We gladly welcome you to our %STRING1.
nodes.trigger: Fires when a Scout enters a native settlement and the 'speak with the chief' outcome is the gift of guides (an expanded map reveal in honor of the visitor's tales).
nodes.inputs: The visiting Scout and the settlement's tribe; a random visit-outcome roll improved by Scout/Seasoned-Scout status.
nodes.outputs: The village provides guides that reveal a larger area of the map around the settlement ("...the {tribe} shall provide you with guides to aid your passage through our lands.").

nodes.label: CHIEFHOWDY
nodes.summary: "Greetings, travelers.  We are a peaceful village
nodes.trigger: Fires when a unit first makes contact with / enters a peaceful native settlement that wants to trade: the village describes its specialty and the goods it needs.
nodes.inputs: The visiting unit and the settlement's tribe; the settlement's specialty good and the commodities it wants to buy/sell (from the per-settlement trade tables).
nodes.outputs: An informational greeting naming the village's specialty and the goods it will trade for ("We are a peaceful village known for our {specialty}. We would gladly trade with you if you bring us some {needed good}..."); no immediate state change beyond opening trade.

nodes.label: CHIEFKILL
nodes.summary: "You have broken sacred taboos of the {%STRING0} tribe!
nodes.trigger: Fires when a unit enters a native settlement under conditions the tribe treats as taboo-breaking (a hostile/forbidden approach), and the village turns on the visitor instead of welcoming it.
nodes.inputs: The attacking unit's index, the attacker's power, the target settlement and its population (the NativeSettlement population field); the difficulty level (sets the per-roll upper bound).
nodes.outputs: The village declares the visitor has broken sacred taboos ("You have broken sacred taboos of the {tribe} tribe! We shall tie you up for target practice."). When this resolves as a raze, gold is awarded to the attacker = (three rolls of 1..(10-difficulty) summed) x (roll of 1..6) x 4 x (settlement population + 1); a capital adds a separate bonus on top.

nodes.label: DEADCONVERTS
nodes.summary: Indian {converts} lose faith and return to tribe.  Converts
nodes.trigger: Fires when an Indian convert working in the field finishes its outdoor work order: the per-unit work counter ticks past 8 turns on a free-colonist (convert) unit whose activity byte marks it as working. Mirrors the rule that converts who do not settle into a colony within eight turns of conversion lose faith.
nodes.inputs: The convert unit's record (type = free colonist, activity = working, plus its work-progress counter), its tile ownership, and whether the owning power is a live human player.
nodes.outputs: The terrain-change work is applied for a human owner, the work order is finished, the convert is consumed/returned to the tribe, and the boxed "Indian converts lose faith and return to tribe" notice is shown.

nodes.label: EXTINCT
nodes.summary: The %STRING0 tribe has been wiped out.
nodes.trigger: Fires when a native tribe loses its last settlement: removing a settlement decrements the tribe's settlement count, and when that count reaches zero the tribe is eliminated.
nodes.inputs: The settlement being removed and its owning tribe; the tribe's remaining settlement-count byte after the removal decrement.
nodes.outputs: The tribe is flagged as eliminated (its record's eliminated bit is set) and the "The {tribe} tribe has been wiped out." announcement is shown.

nodes.label: HEATHEN
nodes.summary: "We are currently busy subduing the notorious heathen {%STRING1} tribe.
nodes.trigger: Shown during a meeting with a native tribe that is at war with another (heathen) tribe and asks the player, as a fellow believer, to join in subduing that rival tribe.
nodes.inputs: The two powers in the meeting (the asking tribe and the player) and the named heathen tribe being subdued; the meeting/relation state.
nodes.outputs: Presents the request ("...Will you, as fellow believers, join with us in this holy task?" -> refuse / "teach the {tribe} a lesson"). The player's choice colors relations: refusing protects the targeted tribe, agreeing aligns the player against it.

nodes.label: HERESY0
nodes.summary: {%STRING0 missionaries} denounce heresy of {%STRING1}.
nodes.trigger: Fires when a missionary of one nation founds/operates a mission in a settlement that already holds a RIVAL nation's mission, and the rival's converts are NOT loyal: the newcomer denounces the rival's heresy and the converts side with the newcomer.
nodes.inputs: The challenging and incumbent mission nations and the settlement's converts (the loyalty roll deciding the outcome).
nodes.outputs: The converts burn the incumbent nation's mission and erect a new mission for the challenging nation ("{nation} missionaries denounce heresy of {rival}. {tribe} converts burn {rival} mission and erect a new, {nation} one!"); the settlement's mission flag flips to the challenging nation.

nodes.label: HERESY1
nodes.summary: {%STRING0 missionaries} denounce heresy of {%STRING1}.
nodes.trigger: Fires in the same mission-rivalry contest as HERESY0 but when the incumbent nation's converts ARE loyal: the challenge fails and the challenger's missionary is killed.
nodes.inputs: The challenging and incumbent mission nations and the settlement's converts (the loyalty roll resolves in the incumbent's favor).
nodes.outputs: The loyal worshipers burn the challenger at the stake ("{nation} missionaries denounce heresy of {rival}. Loyal {tribe} worshipers burn the {nation} at the stake!"); the incumbent mission is retained and the challenging missionary is lost.

nodes.label: INDIANBEGFOOD
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} tribe has fallen upon hard times and does
nodes.trigger: One outcome of the 'speak with the chief' / native-settlement visit dialog: the tribe has fallen on hard times and asks the player to share food.
nodes.inputs: The visiting unit, the settlement, and a mode flag; a random outcome roll gated by settlement size and tribe attitude; the player's food stores.
nodes.outputs: The tribe asks for food ("...Will our brothers of {power} share the bounty of their harvests...") and the player may decline or give an offered quantity of food. On giving, food is transferred from the player to the tribe (amount data-resident, not yet decoded).

nodes.label: INDIANBOW
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} tribe bows before the might of the {%STRING1}.
nodes.trigger: Fires when a tribe submits to a far stronger power after a decisive defeat/intimidation: the tribe bows and cedes its land in tribute.
nodes.inputs: The submitting tribe and the dominant power; the combat/intimidation outcome in the colony-attack resolver tail.
nodes.outputs: The tribe gives the power all the land it occupies ("The {tribe} tribe bows before the might of the {power}... we give you all the land you now occupy."); the land is ceded to the player.

nodes.label: INDIANBRIBE
nodes.summary: "Very well, we withdraw our objection."
nodes.trigger: The player issues a build order (colony, road, or plow) on a tile that a native tribe owns, and chooses to pay the tribe rather than abandon the order. Shown after the tribe's objection prompt when the player agrees to settle the matter.
nodes.inputs: The active unit's tile and the adjacent NativeSettlement's owning tribe; the tribe's standing objection to construction on its land; the player's gold (the bribe cost is read from a per-tribe land table, exact amount not byte-resolved).
nodes.outputs: The tribe withdraws its objection ("Very well, we withdraw our objection."); the build order is allowed to proceed on the contested tile and the tile is marked as conceded to the player. Gold is debited as the bribe (amount not yet decoded).

nodes.label: INDIANBURN
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} burn {%STRING1} missions!  Church authorities
nodes.trigger: Fires when a native tribe destroys the player's missions during a relation/turn change: the settlement-marker refresh scans the tribe's settlements and finds missions belonging to the affected colony to clear.
nodes.inputs: The target tribe index and the player colony index; each NativeSettlement's owner field and mission flag (the low nibble identifying which power's mission it holds).
nodes.outputs: Every matching mission flag is reset to "no mission" (the missions are burned), the tribe's village markers are redrawn, and for a real player colony the "{tribe} burn {power} missions! Church authorities are outraged!" notice is shown.

nodes.label: INDIANBURNCOLONY
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} massacre {%STRING1} colonists at {%STRING3}!
nodes.trigger: Fires when natives win an attack on the HUMAN player's colony decisively enough to destroy it: the colony is massacred and burned to the ground.
nodes.inputs: The attacking native unit and the defending player colony; the land-combat win/loss roll (random over attacker+defender strength, win if roll <= attacker strength) resolving as a native win against the colony.
nodes.outputs: The colony is burned and its colonists massacred ("{tribe} massacre {power} colonists at {colony}! Colony burned to the ground! King demands explanation!"); the colony is removed.

nodes.label: INDIANBURNCOLONY2
nodes.summary: Spies report: {%STRING0} burn {%STRING1} colony at {%STRING3}.
nodes.trigger: The spy-reported (non-human / observed) variant of a native attack that burns a colony to the ground.
nodes.inputs: The attacking tribe and the destroyed colony (a colony not belonging to the active human player); the same native-win combat outcome.
nodes.outputs: Reports the colony's destruction via spies ("Spies report: {tribe} burn {power} colony at {colony}. {power} governor vows revenge."); the colony is removed.

nodes.label: INDIANCITY
nodes.summary: The {%STRING0} settlers in {%STRING3} have committed
nodes.trigger: One outcome of the native-settlement visit dialog (or a tribe grievance): the tribe accuses the player's colonists of destruction and demands reparations from the colony stores, threatening force.
nodes.inputs: The tribe, the offending colony, the commodity and quantity demanded as reparations, and the colony's stockpile of that commodity.
nodes.outputs: Presents the demand ("...we therefore demand {qty} {commodity} from the colony stores as reparations." -> Man the stockade / Hand them over). On Hand them over, the commodity is removed from the colony stores; on Man the stockade, the player risks war.

nodes.label: INDIANCOME
nodes.summary: "We hope you will soon {visit} %STRING0 villages to
nodes.trigger: Drawn as part of the native-tribe relations report toward a power when the tribe's trade/familiarity value is still low (below threshold) -- an invitation to visit and trade.
nodes.inputs: The power index and the tribe handle; the per-(tribe,power) relation/trade value (only drawn when that value is under the threshold).
nodes.outputs: Adds the invitation line "We hope you will soon visit {tribe} villages... and send your wagon trains to trade with us." to the relations display. Informational; no game-state change.

nodes.label: INDIANCOMMENT
nodes.summary: The {%STRING0} are pleased to see the prosperity of our
nodes.trigger: One outcome of the native-settlement visit dialog: a peaceful tribe warns the player that their colonies are overusing land near native settlements.
nodes.inputs: The tribe and the neighboring player; the proximity/land-use pressure of the player's colonies near the tribe's settlements.
nodes.outputs: Shows the warning "...your colonies are beginning to overuse the lands near our settlements." -- a diplomatic caution with no immediate transfer; tension toward the player rises if the behavior continues.

nodes.label: INDIANGIVEFOOD
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} see that your food stores are low this
nodes.trigger: One outcome of the native-settlement visit dialog when the player's food stores are low and the tribe is friendly: the tribe brings a gift of food.
nodes.inputs: The tribe, the player and a player colony; the player's low food state and the tribe's surplus harvest (and the friendly relation).
nodes.outputs: The tribe gifts a stated quantity of food ("We offer you a gift of {qty} food in recognition of the everlasting peace..."); that food is credited to the player.

nodes.label: INDIANGIVESTUFF
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} tribe is pleased to see the progress of
nodes.trigger: One outcome of the native-settlement visit dialog when the tribe is friendly and pleased with a player colony's progress: a gift of trade goods.
nodes.inputs: The tribe, the player colony, and the commodity/quantity gifted (from the settlement's trade tables); the friendly relation.
nodes.outputs: The tribe gifts a stated quantity of a commodity ("We have come to offer you {qty} {commodity} in recognition of the everlasting peace..."); that commodity is credited to the player's colony.

nodes.label: INDIANLOSE
nodes.summary: {%STRING1 %STRING2} %STRING4 {%STRING0} near %STRING3!
nodes.trigger: Fires when a native attack on a defended target is repelled (the defender wins the land-combat roll against the native attacker).
nodes.inputs: The native attacker and the defending unit; the combat roll resolving against the native.
nodes.outputs: The native attack fails near the target ("{defender unit} {verb} {tribe} near {place}!"); the native unit is demoted/destroyed by the combat applier.

nodes.label: INDIANPEACE
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} welcome peace with our brothers
nodes.trigger: Drawn in the native-tribe relations report for an established friendly/peace relationship between the power and the tribe.
nodes.inputs: The power index and tribe handle; the relation query for the treaty/peace bit.
nodes.outputs: Adds the friendship line "The {tribe} welcome peace with our brothers the {power}. Let us smoke a peace pipe..." to the relations display. Informational; reflects the existing peace state.

nodes.label: INDIANSCONVERT
nodes.summary: "The wisdom of your missionaries has convinced some of us
nodes.trigger: One outcome of the native-settlement visit dialog: the tribe, persuaded by the player's missionaries, offers some of its people as converts to join a player colony.
nodes.inputs: The visiting unit/missionary influence, the settlement, and the target player colony; the conversion roll.
nodes.outputs: Some natives join the player colony as converts ("...convinced some of us to join your colony at {colony} and live among you as converts."); one or more convert units are produced for the player.

nodes.label: INDIANSHUN
nodes.summary: "Then the mighty {%STRING0} shall mercilessly drive you from our
nodes.trigger: Outcome of a native interaction (visit/treaty) where the tribe rejects the player and turns hostile: the tribe declares it will drive the player out.
nodes.inputs: The tribe and the player; the tribe's hostile attitude state at the time of the interaction.
nodes.outputs: The tribe declares war ("Then the mighty {tribe} shall mercilessly drive you from our shores. Prepare for WAR!"); the tribe-vs-player relation becomes at-war.

nodes.label: INDIANSLAVES
nodes.summary: Frightened {%STRING0} flock to %STRING1 mission as {converts}.
nodes.trigger: Fires after a native settlement is overcome (e.g. its mission/defenders), when frightened natives flee to a player mission and become converts.
nodes.inputs: The affected tribe and the receiving player mission; the post-combat / mission outcome.
nodes.outputs: Frightened natives join the player's mission as converts ("Frightened {tribe} flock to {power} mission as converts."); convert units are produced for the player.

nodes.label: INDIANSURPRISE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} make surprise raid near {%STRING1}!  Colonists
nodes.trigger: Fires during the native per-unit AI turn when an AI-controlled brave's best-scoring action is a hostile strike whose target is the human player. The native's accumulated alarm/tension toward that power (and/or the value of the goods the player trades) pushes the unit to attack.
nodes.inputs: The acting native unit and its 8 neighbour tiles; the per-(settlement,power) alarm/tension accumulator (a hostile strike becomes attractive once alarm crosses its high threshold) and the market value of coveted cargo; the player colony near the strike.
nodes.outputs: The unit commits a surprise raid near the player's colony and the "{tribe} make surprise raid near {colony}! Colonists frightened. {tribe} chief denies involvement." prompt is shown to the human player; the unit's move order and direction are set toward the target.

nodes.label: INDIANWAGONS
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} settlers have committed
nodes.trigger: A tribe grievance variant of the reparations demand aimed at the player's wagon trains: the tribe accuses the colonists of destruction and demands the goods carried in the wagons.
nodes.inputs: The tribe, the offending colony/wagons, the commodity and quantity carried in the wagons.
nodes.outputs: Presents the demand ("...we therefore demand all {qty} of the {commodity} in these wagons as reparations." -> Hand them over / Circle the wagons). On Hand them over, the wagon cargo is surrendered to the tribe; on Circle the wagons, the player risks attack.

nodes.label: INDIANWARFARE
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} nation holds War Council!
nodes.trigger: Fires when a tribe is incited to war (a war council is held) -- typically driven by a rival nation's missionaries inciting the tribe against another power.
nodes.inputs: The inciting nation, the target nation, and the tribe being incited; the relation/alarm state between the tribe and the target.
nodes.outputs: The tribe holds a War Council and goes to war against the named target ("{tribe} nation holds War Council! {nation} missionaries incite {tribe} to warfare against the {target}!"); the relation/war state between that tribe and the target is set hostile.

nodes.label: INDIANWARPATH2
nodes.summary: "We will gladly drive the {%STRING0} from our ancestral
nodes.trigger: Fires when a Scout asks a native tribe to make war on a specified enemy and the tribe agrees for a price: a paid 'go on the warpath' offer.
nodes.inputs: The player's treasury (PowerRecord gold), the requested enemy tribe, and the computed bribe price (built from a per-power markup/cost chain); affordability is checked before the deal.
nodes.outputs: The tribe offers to drive the named enemy out in exchange for a stated sum ("We will gladly drive the {enemy} from our ancestral lands in exchange for {amount}." -> Pay/Never mind). On Pay, the gold is debited from the player and the tribe goes to war with the target.

nodes.label: INDIANWELCOME
nodes.summary: "The {%STRING0} tribe welcomes you.
nodes.trigger: One outcome of the native-settlement visit dialog: a friendly tribe welcomes the player, offers the occupied land as a gift, and proposes a peace treaty.
nodes.inputs: The visiting unit, the settlement, the tribe and its population/size; the friendly attitude state.
nodes.outputs: The tribe offers the land the player occupies and a peace treaty ("...we generously offer you the land you now occupy as a gift. Will you accept our treaty and live with us in peace as brothers?" -> Yes/No). On Yes, a peace treaty is established and the land is conceded.

nodes.label: INDIANWIN0
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} ambush {%STRING1 %STRING2} near %STRING3!
nodes.trigger: Fires when natives win a field ambush against a player's unit/stack (not a colony) -- the native attacker wins the land-combat roll.
nodes.inputs: The attacking tribe and the ambushed player unit/group near a place; the land-combat roll resolving as a native win.
nodes.outputs: The natives ambush and defeat the player's unit ("{tribe} ambush {player unit} near {place}!"); the player's unit is removed/demoted by the combat applier.

nodes.label: INDIANWINCOLONY
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} massacre {%STRING1} colonists at {%STRING3}!
nodes.trigger: Fires when natives win an attack on the HUMAN player's colony but a defender dies holding it off (a costly successful native assault, colony not razed).
nodes.inputs: The attacking tribe, the player colony, and the named defending colonist who falls; the native-win combat outcome.
nodes.outputs: The colonists are massacred and a defender dies ("{tribe} massacre {power} colonists at {colony}! {defender} dies fending off onslaught.").

nodes.label: INDIANWINCOLONY2
nodes.summary: Spies report: {%STRING0} massacre {%STRING1} colonists at {%STRING3}.
nodes.trigger: The spy-reported (observed / non-human) variant of a native massacre at a colony.
nodes.inputs: The attacking tribe and the colony massacred (not the active human's); the native-win combat outcome.
nodes.outputs: Reports the massacre via spies ("Spies report: {tribe} massacre {power} colonists at {colony}. {power} governor plans countermeasures.").

nodes.label: LOOT
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} loot and burn {%STRING1 %STRING2}!  Natives flee in
nodes.trigger: Fires when the player loots and burns a native settlement that yields a large treasure (a treasure too big to carry without a Galleon).
nodes.inputs: The razed native settlement and the attacker; the recovered treasure amount.
nodes.outputs: The settlement is burned, the natives flee, and a stated treasure is recovered ("{tribe} loot and burn {settlement}! Natives flee in panic! {amount} worth of treasure recovered from ruins! It will take a Galleon to get this treasure back to Europe!"); a treasure unit/value is created for the player.

nodes.label: LOOT2
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} burn {%STRING1 %STRING2}!  Natives flee in panic!
nodes.trigger: Fires when the player loots and burns a native settlement that yields no treasure: the settlement is destroyed but nothing of value is recovered.
nodes.inputs: The razed native settlement and the attacker; a treasure roll resolving to nothing.
nodes.outputs: The settlement is burned and the natives flee with no treasure ("{tribe} burn {settlement}! Natives flee in panic!"); the settlement is removed.

nodes.label: MEEKNESS
nodes.summary: request
nodes.trigger: Not an event message but a phrase fragment ("request"/"demand") used to compose the tone of a native attitude/diplomacy menu line; drawn while building the native attitude menu.
nodes.inputs: The menu anchor position and a 0/1 selector that picks 'request' vs 'demand' (sets the iteration count 1 or 2).
nodes.outputs: Emits the chosen 'request' or 'demand' wording into the rendered native attitude/diplomacy menu line. UI-only; no game-state change.

nodes.label: MISSION0
nodes.summary: %STRING0 %STRING1 mission founded in %STRING2, %NUMBER0.
nodes.trigger: Fires when a missionary establishes a new mission in a native settlement (the mission is founded that turn).
nodes.inputs: The founding power and the native settlement; the settlement's tribe; the current year. (This handler also recomputes the commodity-trade pressure tied to the settlement.)
nodes.outputs: A mission of the founding nation is founded in the settlement ("{nation} {denomination} mission founded in {settlement}, {year}. {tribe} approach new religion with curiosity."); the settlement's mission flag is set to that power and its trade state updates.

nodes.label: RAIDBURN
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} raiding party burns buildings in {%STRING1}!
nodes.trigger: One outcome of a native brave's raid on a player colony, selected by the raid-outcome roll (1..4 remapped by difficulty/feasibility): the raiders burn buildings.
nodes.inputs: The raiding native unit (combat types) and the target colony; the outcome roll and feasibility predicates.
nodes.outputs: Buildings in the colony are destroyed ("{tribe} raiding party burns buildings in {colony}! {building} destroyed. Colonists demand immediate vengeance!"); the named building is removed and a vengeance/alarm effect on the colonists follows.

nodes.label: RAIDGOLD
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} raiding party seizes strongboxes in {%STRING1}!
nodes.trigger: One outcome of a native raid on a player colony (the loot-gold branch), selected by the raid-outcome roll after the gold-poor guard.
nodes.inputs: The raiding tribe's strength, the target colony's size, and the victim power's treasury (these feed the 32-bit loot amount); whether the victim is human.
nodes.outputs: Gold is plundered from the colony: the looted amount is subtracted from the victim power's treasury and recorded for the popup ("{tribe} raiding party seizes strongboxes in {colony}! Merchants report {amount} plundered. Colonists enraged!").

nodes.label: RAIDNOTHING
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} raiding party wiped out in {%STRING1}!
nodes.trigger: The 'no effect' outcome of a native raid on a player colony, selected when the outcome roll resolves to nothing (e.g. the raiding party is repelled).
nodes.inputs: The raiding native unit and the target colony; the outcome roll resolving to the NOTHING branch.
nodes.outputs: The raid fails with no loss to the player ("{tribe} raiding party wiped out in {colony}! Colonists jubilant!"); the per-(raider,victim) raid-tension counter is cleared.

nodes.label: RAIDSHIP
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} raiding party attacks harbor in {%STRING1}!
nodes.trigger: One outcome of a native raid on a coastal player colony: the raiders attack a ship in the harbor.
nodes.inputs: The raiding native unit, the target colony, and a ship docked there; the outcome roll selecting the ship/harbor branch.
nodes.outputs: A ship in the harbor is damaged ("{tribe} raiding party attacks harbor in {colony}! {ship} damaged. Colonists appalled!").

nodes.label: RAIDSTORES
nodes.summary: {%STRING0} raiding party attacks stores in {%STRING1}!
nodes.trigger: One outcome of a native raid on a player colony: the raiders steal from the colony stores.
nodes.inputs: The raiding native unit and the target colony's stockpile; the outcome roll selecting the STORES branch (gated by a feasibility predicate).
nodes.outputs: A commodity is stolen from the colony stores ("{tribe} raiding party attacks stores in {colony}! Large quantities of {commodity} stolen. Colonists outraged!"); the raid path also bumps the target settlement's wealth/aggression accumulators.

nodes.label: RAIDWREAK
nodes.summary: Spies report: {%STRING0} raiding party wreaks havoc in
nodes.trigger: The population/general-havoc outcome of a native raid on a (often AI-owned, spy-reported) player colony.
nodes.inputs: The raiding native unit and the target colony; the outcome roll selecting the WREAK/population branch.
nodes.outputs: The raiding party wreaks havoc on the colony, reported via spies ("Spies report: {tribe} raiding party wreaks havoc in the {power} colony of {colony}.").

nodes.label: SMITEINDIANS
nodes.summary: "We shall ruthlessly smite the heathen {%STRING0}
nodes.trigger: Shown when the player, in a meeting, asks a native tribe to attack ("smite") another heathen tribe in exchange for payment.
nodes.inputs: The attacker power's treasury and the opponent/target tribe; a player-factor table and the tribe's treasury feed the loot/cost computation; the bit-19 power attribute can halve the amount.
nodes.outputs: Offers to smite the named tribe for a stated sum ("We shall ruthlessly smite the heathen {tribe} in exchange for {amount}." -> Pay/Never mind). On Pay (and if the payer can afford it) the gold transfers between the involved powers; otherwise the UNFORTUNATE refusal is shown.

nodes.label: WANTSTUFF
nodes.summary: "We are displeased that you continue to befoul lands that are
nodes.trigger: Shown when a native tribe (or power), in a meeting, demands a commodity from the player as reparations for befouling land it claims.
nodes.inputs: The demanding tribe, the player, the commodity and quantity demanded, and the player's holdings of that commodity; gated on the running attitude score and the best-good index.
nodes.outputs: Presents the demand ("...We demand {qty} {commodity} as reparations." -> mock them / "gladly share {qty} {commodity}"). On comply, the commodity is moved between the two powers' market arrays; on refusal, tension/war risk rises.

nodes.label: WHACKINDIANS
nodes.summary: Shall we attack the {%STRING0}, Your Excellency?
nodes.trigger: The player commands one of their units to attack a tile occupied by a native tribe with whom no war is yet declared (relation "at war" bit clear). A Yes/No confirmation is raised before committing the attack.
nodes.inputs: The acting unit and the target tile's occupant tribe; the current relation flags between the player and that tribe (treaty/peace bits); whether the acting power is human.
nodes.outputs: On Yes ("Shall we attack the {tribe}?" -> Yes), war is declared: the war bit is set in the relation matrix for the player toward that tribe and the existing treaty/peace bit is cleared, after which the attack proceeds. On No, nothing changes.

nodes.label: LOSENOCOLONIES
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 %STRING1.  Our efforts in the New World have
nodes.trigger: End-of-turn king check: from the year 1600 onward, the player has zero colonies and is not in the War of Independence.
nodes.inputs: The active power's colony count (zero), the current year (>= 1600), the war flag (not at war), the player's leader title and name.
nodes.outputs: The King removes the player as Viceroy ('Our efforts in the New World have proven fruitless...'); the score result is zeroed and the game ends in defeat.

nodes.label: SCORE
nodes.summary: An Infectious Disease, %STRING0 Fever
nodes.trigger: End of game: the score/Hall-of-Fame screen is shown and computes the player's rank, which selects a legacy-naming line.
nodes.inputs: The raw per-power score (population, colonies, founding fathers, gold, bells, etc. - see note), the difficulty factor (Discoverer/Explorer/Conquistador/Governor/Viceroy map to 4/5/6/8/10), and the player/leader name. Rank 0-23 is found via pct = factor*raw_score/100 binned through a quadratic ladder ((k*k)/3 < pct), clamped to 23. The factor math and rank ladder are byte-verified; the raw-score component WEIGHTS live in an overlay routine and are NOT verified (do not trust the reconstructed SCORING.md formula).
nodes.outputs: Picks one entry from the legacy list (a Fever / Fly / Ivy / Rattlesnake / ...Boulevard / ...Mountains / Republic of... / ...ica) keyed by the computed rank, naming something after the player, and draws the rank title (@SCORE1..@SCORE24) plus the medallion sprite.

nodes.label: VICEROY
nodes.trigger: Start of a new game: the opening 'Audience With The King' investiture screen where the monarch dubs the player Viceroy of the New World.
nodes.inputs: The chosen nation/country name and the nation index (Netherlands shows the 'Stadtholder' variant @VICEROY2 instead of 'The King').
nodes.outputs: Displays the dub-thee-Viceroy address ('For the greater glory of {country}, we dub thee Viceroy of the New World...') in a year-1492 audience panel; on Netherlands an alternate Stadtholder clause is appended.

nodes.label: ARMOPTIONS
nodes.summary: Don't get on next ship.
nodes.trigger: Player clicks a unit on the European dock/harbor to open its options menu.
nodes.inputs: Selected unit's type, the costs to arm/equip with Muskets, Tools, or Horses (and the sale credits), and whether it can be blessed as a missionary.
nodes.outputs: Shows the dock-options menu: board/skip next ship, move to front of dock, arm/sell Muskets, equip/sell Tools, equip/sell Horses, bless/cancel Missionary status, or no changes.

nodes.label: LOADGAME
nodes.summary: Select Game To Load
nodes.trigger: Player chooses Load Game from the menu, opening the load-slot picker.
nodes.inputs: Available save files in the slots; the load command is gated by the LOADGAME message key; each file's COLONIZE magic, version, and map size are validated.
nodes.outputs: Shows the 'Select Game To Load' dialog; on a chosen slot it runs the load driver and maps the result to a message (LOADGOOD / LOADNOT / LOADOLD / LOADSIZE / LOADERROR).

nodes.label: MAPTOLOAD
nodes.summary: ^^Select Map File to Load
nodes.trigger: Player starts a game in AMERICA and chooses 'Map Editor' (custom map), opening the .MP map-file picker.
nodes.inputs: The list of available '*.MP' map files in the save/data directory; menu keys OPENMENU/BEGINMENU/AMERICA drive the surrounding screen.
nodes.outputs: Shows the 'Select Map File to Load' header and file list; the chosen .MP map name is recorded (replacing the default AMER2.MP) and loaded.

nodes.label: MULTI
nodes.summary: ^^Multiplayer Start Selected
nodes.trigger: Multiplayer start is selected (via the COLONIZE_MULTI environment variable or a command-line/menu option), prompting selection of human-controlled powers.
nodes.inputs: The COLONIZE_MULTI env var (compared against 'MULTI'), command-line argv option markers; the active-power roster.
nodes.outputs: Shows the 'Multiplayer Start Selected' screen and lets the player pick which European powers are controlled by human players.

nodes.label: NATION0A
nodes.summary: ^^ENGLAND
nodes.trigger: New-game initialization draws the leader/nation intro panel after the starting European power is chosen (randomly picked 0-3 unless multiplayer).
nodes.inputs: The randomly chosen nation index (England/France/Spain/Netherlands), the leader-name string, and the chosen nation's history/description text section.
nodes.outputs: Composes the intro panel (WOODPANL background + LEADERNAME prompt + the NATION0A-family nation description text) and zero-initializes the per-power PowerRecord and AIPersonality tables.

nodes.label: REALLYBUY
nodes.summary: Purchase %STRING0 for %NUMBER0$?
nodes.trigger: Player confirms a purchase action that costs gold (e.g. buying a recruit, specialist, or item) and the game asks for final confirmation.
nodes.inputs: The item/thing being purchased and its gold cost.
nodes.outputs: Yes/No confirmation prompt 'Purchase X for $N?'; on Yes the purchase proceeds and gold is deducted.

nodes.label: SAVEGAME
nodes.summary: Select Save Slot
nodes.trigger: Player chooses Save Game from the menu, opening the save-slot picker.
nodes.inputs: The current game state and the available save slots (filenames built as COLONY<slot>.SAV); the save command is gated by the SAVEGAME message key.
nodes.outputs: Shows the 'Select Save Slot' dialog; on a chosen slot it invokes the save driver to write the COLONIZE-magic save file, then reports success (SAVEGOOD) or an error (SAVEERROR).

nodes.label: TRIBUTE
nodes.summary: "%STRING0 has told us that we must drive all {%STRING1} from the
nodes.trigger: During a European-power diplomacy meeting, the other (e.g. Catholic) power offers to overlook your colonies in exchange for a gold 'donation'.
nodes.inputs: The demanding power's sponsor name, the natives/region cited, your colony location, and the demanded donation amount in gold; your treasury.
nodes.outputs: Presents the demand: refuse ('Not a penny for those heretic swine') or pay the donation; paying transfers the gold and avoids hostility.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL1
nodes.summary: Our {%STRING0} carrying a pioneer and a soldier is on the high seas,
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints option is on and, on the very first turn (Discoverer level), the player's ship carrying a pioneer and soldier is selected on the high seas; shown once.
nodes.inputs: Active unit and its type/owner, turn counter (turn 0), difficulty (Discoverer), the per-hint shown bit, and whether the ship is on screen.
nodes.outputs: Pops a hint box explaining to sail west (left arrow) to find land or east (right arrow) to return to port, then sets the hint's shown bit so it never repeats.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL10
nodes.summary: This looks like a good place to {plow} or {clear}.  Our {pioneers} will plow
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a pioneer is on a tile that is a good place to plow or clear (forest/terrain band, >=2 forest neighbours).
nodes.inputs: Active pioneer position, 8-neighbour forest/terrain-band count; shown-bit.
nodes.outputs: Hint box explaining plowing (press 'P'): plowing raises food/tobacco/cotton/sugar by one, and plowing a forest clears it for agriculture.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL11
nodes.summary: Our ship, a {%STRING0}, is one of our most valuable units.  We can use
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: early game (turn < 20), the player's ship is selected, explaining what ships are for; shown once.
nodes.inputs: Active unit type/cargo, turn counter, the ship's type name and home port; shown-bit.
nodes.outputs: Hint box describing the ship's uses (explore, carry cargo home, bring immigrants) and controls (arrow keys, 'G' to send to a port).

nodes.label: TUTORIAL12
nodes.summary: Our ship has arrived in %STRING0, Your Excellency, and is waiting
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: the player opens the colony screen of a port colony where a ship is waiting for cargo (first-visit block B with a ship-type unit present).
nodes.inputs: Active colony, presence of a ship-type defender (unit type in the ship band) at the colony, the colony name; shown-bit.
nodes.outputs: Hint box explaining how to drag warehouse cargo into the ship's holds, return to the map (ESC), then send the ship to Europe with 'G'.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL13
nodes.summary: Our {pioneers} have arrived in the New World, Excellency!  They are
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: early game (turn < 20), the player's pioneers (type 2) have just arrived in the New World and have no feature yet; shown once.
nodes.inputs: Active unit type (pioneers), turn counter, whether the tile has a feature; shown-bit.
nodes.outputs: Hint box advising to find a coastal site with food/resources for the first colony, noting pioneers carry 100 Tools for clearing/plowing/roads.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL14
nodes.summary: Our {soldiers} have two uses.  They can be used to attack our
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: early game (turn < 20), the player's soldiers (type 1) have arrived with no feature yet; shown once.
nodes.inputs: Active unit type (soldiers), turn counter, tile feature flag; shown-bit.
nodes.outputs: Hint box explaining soldiers attack and defend, carry 50 Muskets, and become stronger when equipped with Horses.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL15
nodes.summary: New colonists have arrived in {%STRING0}, Your Excellency!  You can make
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: new colonists have arrived in a colony (turn < 40), prompting the player to assign them.
nodes.inputs: Active unit type (colonist, type 0), turn counter, the destination colony record/name; shown-bit.
nodes.outputs: Hint box telling the player to click the colony and drag the new colonists from the fence into a field or building.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL19
nodes.summary: {Converts} are natives who for one reason or another have decided to
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a colonist of type 0 is on/near specific terrain (converts context), explaining native Converts; shown once.
nodes.inputs: Active unit type and the terrain under it; shown-bit.
nodes.outputs: Hint box explaining Converts (natives who join your colonies): they cannot be educated but are better at farming, planting, fishing, and mining.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL2
nodes.summary: We've found uncharted land, Excellency.  To put the colonists ashore,
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: shown when the ship has found uncharted land and the player should disembark.
nodes.inputs: Active ship unit position relative to land; tutorial shown-bit.
nodes.outputs: Hint box telling the player to move the ship toward land and choose Make Landfall to put colonists ashore.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL3
nodes.summary: The abundance of {%STRING0} in this area makes this a good place to
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a pioneer is on a tile whose surroundings have abundant resources and at least ~5 nearby land tiles, suggesting a first colony site; shown once.
nodes.inputs: Active unit position, 8/9-neighbour terrain scan (land/colony counts via terrain-id and colony-index lookups), the named resource of the area; shown-bit.
nodes.outputs: Hint box saying the abundance here makes a good first-colony spot and to press 'B' to build; sets the shown bit.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL4
nodes.summary: On the {Colony Screen}, you can decide what the colonists in this colony
nodes.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: the player opens the Colony Screen for the very first time (first-visit block in the colony dialog).
nodes.inputs: Active colony, its current worker and what it produces, an empty surrounding ring tile; shown-bit on the colony-screen-seen flag.
nodes.outputs: Hint box explaining the Colony Screen and Jobs Menu (change a colonist's job, drag him to a tile/building, or to the fence to remove him); sets the seen bit.

nodes.label: TUTORIAL5
